detail.abstract: This paper examines the statistical structure of annual institutional change using the full country coverage of the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI), 1996-2024. A composite institutional index is constructed for 216 countries and territories from the six WGI dimensions, and year-on-year change in this index is analyzed across 5,265 country-year transitions. Because WGI estimates carry country-specific margins of error that are substantially larger for states with sparse source coverage, the analysis is conducted in parallel on the full sample and on a reliability-conditioned subsample of 162 countries selected using WGI's own standard-error data. The two samples yield materially different distributional pictures. In the full sample, extreme values are determined by small states and territories with thin source coverage, producing an unstable, source-driven skew (+1.49) and extreme kurtosis (49.6) that substantially reflect measurement noise rather than institutional dynamics. In the reliabilityconditioned subsample, skewness is statistically indistinguishable from zero (0.005), while excess kurtosis remains large and robust (5.5). Deviations beyond four standard deviations occur roughly 86 times more often than a Gaussian benchmark would predict (Jarque-Bera statistic 5,157, p < .001). Tail events in the reliable sample correspond to well-documented historical episodes

title: Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration in Template-Based Retrosynthesis Models: A Cross-Architecture Study of LocalRetro and MHNreact

detail.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration in Template-Based Retrosynthesis Models: A Cross-Architecture Study of LocalRetro and MHNreact

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, human data, or animals. All analyses were performed computationally on publicly available reaction datasets (USPTO-50K). Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Template-based single-step retrosynthesis models output a softmax distribution over a template vocabulary, and their top score is routinely read as a confidence. We ask whether that built-in signal reliably separates correct from incorrect predictions, and whether the separation survives distribution shift toward rare and novel templates. Across two architecturally distinct models on USPTO-50K (n = 5,007), LocalRetro (a graph neural network) and MHNreact (a Modern Hopfield retrieval network), the answer is no, and the failure takes two distinct forms. LocalRetro is well calibrated in aggregate but collapses sharply under template rarity; MHNreact is more uniformly miscalibrated. The standard perturbation remedies, MC dropout and deep ensembling, do not rescue the rare tail in either model, and in MHNreact both signals are inverted rather than merely uninformative, a boundary-robust and seed-replicated result. Per-tier (Mondrian) conformal selective prediction is the one method that restores error control. Finally, a held-out-reaction-class experiment confirms the collapse under genuine novelty: with two entire reaction classes removed from training, top-1 accuracy falls to 0.00-0.25% while the model remains confident (out-of-distribution ECE up to 0.39), the deployment failure mode that matters most.

title: The Structure of Timing Signals: A Taxonomy of what Exists and Why it Fails
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Structure of Timing Signals: A Taxonomy of what Exists and Why it Fails

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the developer of Temporal Structural Forecasting and a principal of TSF Inc., a Delaware corporation that commercializes the methodology. The paper advances no performance claim and reports no results.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
A timing signal is the instruction that opens a position, and it must state the price the trader will pay and the date the transaction will occur. This paper classifies timing signals on two axes. The first states what the trigger specifies, which is a price, a temporal coordinate, or both. The second states the origin of that number, which convention supplies, a test against a historical series selects, or the historical record produces. Each axis divides into three categories that are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive, and each position in the resulting three by three matrix is the product of its row and its column, so the nine positions stand defined before any timing signal occupies one. 

     An enumeration of the published field places 32 timing signals in the matrix, and they occupy eight of the nine positions. Every occupied position withholds a price, withholds a date, or names a session by its relation to the present rather than by a date on the calendar, and one position states a price that exists only once the session it applies to has closed. Each failure belongs to the position rather than to the timing signal, so no refinement of a timing signal repairs it. No occupied position produces a record of transactions a trader could have executed at the price the timing signal stated. Every result the field has published was therefore constructed by a tester who supplied the withheld component after the outcome had resolved, and every such result reports a return higher than the timing signal could have produced. 

     The remaining position was defined by its row and its column before any placement, so the vacancy is a specification rather than an absence of evidence. A timing signal occupying it publishes a price and the future date on which that price applies, and it publishes both before that date arrives, so a trader places a resting order that fills at the published price or does not fill at all. The public record of the named date establishes which occurred, and no component of the result is supplied by anyone. Temporal Structural Forecasting publishes such a price at such a date.

detail.abstract: The Red Sea corridor carries approximately 12% of global trade, yet it has evolved into a complex geopolitical arena where great power interests, regional ambitions, and logistics competition converge. This paper assesses the potential shift of regional trade from the centralized Dubai hub (Jebel Ali Port) toward a decentralized or direct model centered on Port Sudan. Using a mixed-method analysis of trade data, infrastructure assessments, sanctions frameworks, and geopolitical realignments (2023-2026), the study quantifies potential losses for Jebel Ali and identifies the re-export ecosystem and gold trade as the most vulnerable segments. Three scenarios are developed: continued "creative chaos," the Saudi-led Red Sea integration, and an Eastern rogue route under Russian-Chinese barter systems. The paper concludes that while Jebel Ali will not collapse operationally, the erosion of its value-added services and gold-based financial intermediation poses a long-term strategic threat. Policy recommendations focus on diversification, railway rehabilitation, and sanctions compliance.

title: The Closing Circuit: A Sraffian Model of Self-Reproducing Capital and Monopoly Rent — Class Struggle on the Technological Vector in the Exterminist Phase

detail.title: The Closing Circuit: A Sraffian Model of Self-Reproducing Capital and Monopoly Rent — Class Struggle on the Technological Vector in the Exterminist Phase

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The Sraffa-Morishima-Foley apparatus formalises capitalism as a circuit in which living labour produces all surplus, and the New Interpretation (NI) preserves an aggregate identity between monetary surplus and unpaid labour time. We extend the apparatus to a regime in which a self-reproducing sector V — no living-labour requirement, no inputs from the rest of the economy, monopoly closure on the inputs it sells to H — reproduces itself out of machines. Three results follow. First, aggregate surplus decomposes canonically as Σ = ΣH + ΣV, where ΣV = pVAVHqH is monopoly rent that the NI, applied to the subsystem H in which living labour operates, does not count as unpaid living labour: the decomposition localises the exact share of surplus that escapes the labour-value account (Theorem 2). Second, the phase variable χ = ΣV/Σ is strictly monotone increasing under the perturbations corresponding to the historical expansion of V — a theorem in the scalar, proportional, ε = 0 and nV = 1 cases, a certified theorem under the composite condition Kcomposite in the general vector case, and falsified outside Kcomposite, where the unrestricted form admits documented in-domain counterexamples; χ → 1 is mathematically equivalent to rH → 0. Third, in the exterminist limit eight structural properties of the classical apparatus collapse simultaneously, including a categorial inversion of class-political pressure (∂χ/∂πH > 0): union power exercised within H accelerates the migration of the surplus toward V, and the terrain of class struggle extends to the technological vector itself. The paper separates throughout what is proved from what is not: the companion direction ∂χ/∂πV < 0 is carried by the Part III taxation extension and is not established in the canonical block, and the present economy is calibrated outside the certified region. The precise places where the argument can be attacked are marked, and the replication package resolves every certified number to a specific artefact.

title: Impact of Fiscal Transfers on Local Government Budget Execution in Nepal

detail.title: Impact of Fiscal Transfers on Local Government Budget Execution in Nepal
detail.abstract:
The Constitution of Nepal (2015) introduced Nepal's federal system with the creation of 753 local governments with significant responsibilities for basic service delivery and local development. But the local governments are very dependent on the fiscal transfer from the federal government because of their small own-source revenue. This paper looks at the effect of fiscal transfers on local government budget execution in Nepal. It examines the legal environment of intergovernmental transfers, trends in local budgets and the causes of difficulties faced by many local authorities in effectively spending the resources allocated to them. The study demonstrates, using available data, that transfers constitute the financial backbone of local governments but their timing, predictability and design have a strong impact on the quality of local budget execution. Late release of funds, complex conditionalities, weak local capacity and a rush to spend at the end of the fiscal year diminish the efficiency and quality of public spending. The paper ends with recommendations for strengthening transfer design, enhancing local capacity and improving budget execution for
effectiveness and accountability.

title: Terroir and Territory, GIs as Expression of Sovereignty in Times of Climate Change

detail.title: Terroir and Territory, GIs as Expression of Sovereignty in Times of Climate Change
detail.abstract: Geographical indications (GIs) embody sovereignty by legally connecting products, places, and communities, yet their protection increasingly operates through transnational legal structures. This chapter examines how GI regimes illustrate a broader transformation of sovereignty from territorial independence toward interdependence and shared regulatory authority. It compares the EU’s sui generis system, the U.S. trademark- and market-oriented approach, and China’s evolving hybrid system, while situating them within WTO, WIPO, and bilateral treaty frameworks. Climate change destabilizes the traditional concept of terroir by altering the environmental conditions on which geographical specifications depend, thereby challenging historically fixed boundaries, grape varieties, and production methods. The chapter argues that GI law should respond through periodic specification review, climate-related exceptions, trans-border GIs, flexible sourcing rules, and scientifically justified adaptation. Rather than treating GIs as static expressions of territorial control, it proposes understanding them as forms of living heritage sustained through shared sovereignty and shared stewardship.

title: Improving DJIA Forecasting with Bias-Adjusted ARIMA-GARCH Models: A Comparative Evaluation of Stochastic and Volatility-Scaled Adjustments

detail.title: Improving DJIA Forecasting with Bias-Adjusted ARIMA-GARCH Models: A Comparative Evaluation of Stochastic and Volatility-Scaled Adjustments
detail.abstract: ⎯ This study evaluates three one-step-ahead forecasting approaches for the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA): an MLE-estimated ARIMA (1,0,1)-GARCH (1,1) model, a stochastic bias-adjusted extension using randomly generated positive and negative adjustments, and a Scaled Dynamics Bias Adjustment based on residual volatility. The models are evaluated using December 2024 forecast results and compared across multiple error metrics. Both bias-adjusted approaches reduced forecast errors compared with the baseline MLE + ARIMA model. The stochastic bias adjusted model achieved the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE), while the dynamic approach substantially reduced systematic forecast bias and improved average relative error. These findings suggest that incorporating bias adjustments may improve one-step-ahead DJIA forecasts, particularly under changing market conditions. However, the stochastic nature of the adjustments may produce different forecasts across executions. Future research should therefore consider controlled randomization, Monte Carlo simulations, and larger rolling-origin out-of-sample evaluations to assess the robustness, stability, and generalizability of these approaches.

title: Regulations without Teeth: The Impact of Major Energy User Designation Program in Vietnam
affiliations: Fulbright University Vietnam and Monash University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Regulations without Teeth: The Impact of Major Energy User Designation Program in Vietnam
detail.abstract: To cope with rising energy demand, Vietnam has implemented a program in which firms identified using more than 1,000 tons of oil equivalent (toe) are subjected to several administrative and regulatory measures to improve their energy efficiency since 2011. In this study, we establish the first causal evidence of the impact of the program on energy intensity of manufacturing firms. Employing a fuzzy regression discontinuity design, we show that the program is ineffective in improving energy intensity as measured by the energy content of the output production. Our explanation for its inefficiency points to the largely procedural implementation and the asymmetry between penalties of non-compliance and the cost of proper implementation. We conclude with several key recommendations for future policy improvements.

title: Temperature Shock Volatility
affiliations: Swiss Finance Institute and

detail.title: Temperature Shock Volatility

declarations.funderStatement: Loriano Mancini gratefully acknowledges the financial support from the Swiss Finance Institute and the Swiss National Science Foundation under the SNF grants 100018\_189191 and 100018\_204561.

detail.abstract: We develop a novel framework to estimate the variance and covariance of air temperature shocks nonparametrically. Using a Fourier filter, we remove slow-moving components such as trend and seasonal patterns from temperature data and recover temperature shocks. At the target convergence rate, following a deterministic bias correction, the estimators achieve the asymptotic efficiency of oracle estimators, as if shocks were directly observed, satisfy stable Central Limit Theorems, and admit feasible inference. We apply the estimators to hourly temperature data for 51 densely populated urban areas over the period 1940-2024. While average temperature has an upward trend, temperature shock volatility exhibits an inverse U-shape pattern over 1940-2024, with a sharp decline after the 2000s.

title:
Getting Better: 
Changes in Retiree Income Over Time
affiliations: Investment Company Institute and Investment Company Institute

detail.title:
Getting Better: 
Changes in Retiree Income Over Time
detail.abstract: This paper examines changes in retiree income over time using cross-sectional tax data from 2003 through 2017. Using 2016 cross-sectional data, Brady and Bass (2024) found that median spendable income fell by 1.0% per year of age, on average, from age 70 through age 98. That study also found that the incidence of non-Social-Security retirement income, which held steady at 70% or higher from age 71 through age 91, declined after age 91. These results raise the question of whether these age patterns reflect the typical experience of aging individuals or the different life experiences of each birth-year cohort. This study analyzes synthetic cohorts to disentangle age and cohort effects. We find the decline in income at older ages is a cohort effect. Controlling for birth year, median inflation-adjusted income does not decline with age. For example, individuals born in 1932 had roughly the same median income when aged 85 (in 2017) that they had back when they were aged 71 (in 2003), adjusted for inflation. Nonetheless, their age 71 median income was nearly 20% less than individuals aged 71 in 2017. Similarly, once we control for birth year, we see much more modest declines in the incidence of non-Social-Security retirement income after age 90. Rather than being a cause for concern, the decline in income with age observed in cross-sectional data is consistent with an improvement in retiree income. Our analysis shows that, on average, birth-year cohorts maintained their inflation-adjusted income in retirement but that more recent cohorts entered retirement with higher income. The values plotted in the figures are available in an accompanying Excel spreadsheet.

title: NFOS: An Event-Driven, Execution-Aware Architecture for Multi-Venue Opportunity Discovery in Decentralized Finance

detail.title: NFOS: An Event-Driven, Execution-Aware Architecture for Multi-Venue Opportunity Discovery in Decentralized Finance

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Fredrick Mendez, MBA is Founder & Researcher at Novra, which develops the Novra Financial Operating System (NFOS), and therefore has a commercial and non-financial interest in the system described and evaluated in this manuscript. This relationship is disclosed for transparency. No other competing interests are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants, identifiable personal data, clinical research, or animal subjects and therefore did not require institutional ethics approval
declarations.funderStatement: No external grant funding was received for this study. The research described in this manuscript was conducted within the Novra NFOS research program.

detail.abstract: Decentralized financial markets combine fragmented automated market makers, lending protocols, heterogeneous blockchain execution environments, variable transaction costs, and adversarial transaction ordering. A nominal cross-venue price difference is therefore not equivalent to an executable arbitrage opportunity. This paper presents the Novra Financial Operating System (NFOS), an event-driven and execution-aware architecture designed to connect raw market-state acquisition with canonical asset verification, opportunity normalization, cross-venue route construction, executable-price estimation, liquidity and capital-source evaluation, deterministic profitability controls, simulation, transaction delivery, and post-decision telemetry. The research contribution is a systems formulation in which opportunity quality is defined by executable net economics rather than nominal spread alone, and in which probabilistic intelligence may prioritize candidates while deterministic gates retain execution authority. We report preliminary bounded Arbitrum measurements from an eight-pair evaluation configuration. A pre-correction infrastructure run averaged 142.61 RPC requests per cycle and 7.568 s per cycle, with 192 of 192 evaluations rejected below the net-profit threshold and zero transaction submissions; this run is not used for economic inference because cross-venue selection logic was subsequently corrected. In a post-correction bounded run, distinct-venue routing was verified with zero same-venue routes, Camelot participation and DODO sell-side participation were observed, approximately 213 RPC requests per cycle and approximately 7 s cycle latency were measured, and no positive gross or net opportunity reached submission. The results show that correctness constraints and venue coverage materially affect infrastructure cost and that request-efficiency improvements alone cannot establish economic effectiveness. We define prospective hypotheses, an ablation framework, and publication-grade metrics for testing whether event-driven observation, executable-price ranking, dynamic sizing, and capital routing improve realized opportunity conversion.

title:
The Paradox of Control in Banking Systems: 
Synchronisation of Marginally Binding Constraints, Correlated Responses and Dynamic Amplification

detail.title:
The Paradox of Control in Banking Systems: 
Synchronisation of Marginally Binding Constraints, Correlated Responses and Dynamic Amplification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract:
The systemic-risk literature extensively documents common exposures, constrained deleveraging, fire sales, contagion and macro-financial feedbacks. Dynamic stress tests developed by the European Central Bank explicitly model balance-sheet responses and their second-round effects. The contribution of this paper is not to rediscover these mechanisms. 

It proposes a more specific channel: systemic fragility may arise not necessarily from the homogeneity of prudential rules, but from the synchronisation of Kuhn-Tucker regimes in which such rules become simultaneously marginally binding. A common shock that makes the same types of constraints binding aligns marginal optimisation conditions through the associated Lagrange multipliers and increases the conditional correlation of balance-sheet adjustments (H1). Subject to conditions relating to memory, contagion and the spectral radius of the transmission matrix, this initial correlation then increases the amplitude or persistence of the aggregate response (H2). 

The Lagrange multiplier thus provides the proposed microeconomic mechanism linking an individual constraint to systemic covariance. A structural extension based on the Merton model indicates how the same channel may extend to correlated default probabilities and joint defaults; this quantitative extension is left to a separate study. The present version is a theoretical framework: H1 and H2 are formulated as testable implications but are not estimated empirically in this paper.

title: Instructional Leadership Under Dual-Curriculum Pressure: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework for Bilingual K-12 Schools in China

detail.title: Instructional Leadership Under Dual-Curriculum Pressure: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework for Bilingual K-12 Schools in China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This is a narrative literature review synthesising previously published research. No primary data were collected and no human participants were involved; ethics approval is not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: China now hosts more K-12 schools delivering non-national curricula than any other country, and an increasing share now blend a host-nation curriculum with an English-medium one. This growth has outpaced research into how instructional leaders in these schools manage the resulting dual-curriculum pressure. This narrative review synthesises 14 sources across four strands: the structural and staffing realities of international/bilingual schooling in China, the instructional leadership tradition founded on the Principal Instructional Management Rating Scale (PIMRS), leadership challenges specific to internationally-accredited curricula (e.g. the International Baccalaureate), and emerging scholarship on leader identity in dual-language settings. Based on this synthesis, the review proposes an original conceptual extension: that the PIMRS dimension of 'managing the instructional programme' requires splitting into local-staff and expatriate-staff sub-constructs to adequately describe leadership practice in schools with cotaught bilingual classrooms. This proposition is offered as a conceptual contribution and a direction for future empirical research, not as an empirically tested finding.

title: The Economics of Conditional Grants: Local Health Service Delivery in Nepal's Federal System

detail.title: The Economics of Conditional Grants: Local Health Service Delivery in Nepal's Federal System
detail.abstract:
Fiscal federalism in Nepal has conditional grants as one of its key features. These grants are a way for the federal government to send money to state and local governments for certain purposes, especially for health and education. This paper explores whether conditional health grants translate into better delivery of local health services, or are mostly an administrative burden for local governments. The analysis, which is based on publicly available data from the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission, the Ministry of Health and Population, the Ministry of Finance and international organizations including the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank and the World Health Organization, presents a mixed picture. Conditional health grants have increased local health expenditure and helped to sustain basic health services during Nepal's transition to federalism. For example, local governments now constitute a significant proportion of total public health expenditure and
immunization coverage has been sustained in the face of significant institutional reforms. But
the grant system also creates a lot of administrative work, limits local flexibility, slows the
flow of funds and does not always result in better health outcomes. However, many
municipalities have continued to experience low health grant execution rates and key health
indicators such as stunting and neonatal mortality have not improved significantly. The paper
argues that conditional grants are a transitional mechanism that maintains service continuity
while local governments build their own capacity. It proposes reforms to simplify conditional
grants, increase local discretion through block grants, strengthen performance-based elements
and build local capacity for health planning and financial management. The findings
contribute to the larger literature on intergovernmental transfers and local service delivery in
decentralized systems.

title: Does Flood Affect the Intensity of Livelihood Diversification? A Study in the Flood-Affected Areas of Assam, India
affiliations: and Dibrugarh University

detail.title: Does Flood Affect the Intensity of Livelihood Diversification? A Study in the Flood-Affected Areas of Assam, India
detail.abstract: Diversification of livelihood strategies is one of the most sought livelihood strategies of the people around the globe. People diversify their livelihood due to the uncertainties prevailing around the households. In certain other cases, people diversify their livelihood due to emerging opportunities that arise due to socio-political and economic changes. The Livelihood strategy of the rural people of developing countries is a function of multiple factors ranging from access to resources and vectors of demographic, geographic, and socioeconomic factors. Most of the factors are common in rural areas of India. However, in certain pockets of the country natural calamities affect the livelihood pattern of the people. Flood, being the most severe natural calamities in the state of Assam, has a significant impact on the livelihood strategies of the people of the state. With this backdrop, this study aims at constructing and comparing the livelihood diversification index in the flood-affected areas and the flood-free areas adjacent to the affected areas. The livelihood diversification index for this study is constructed using the Herfindahl-Hirschman index. The livelihood diversification index of the households of the study area is 2.4470. The study finds that the livelihood diversification index of flood-affected areas (2.5196) is significantly higher than the flood-free areas (2.2308).

title: Household Monetary Transmission Architecture

detail.title: Household Monetary Transmission Architecture

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human or animal subjects requiring ethics board approval. All empirical analysis uses publicly available, de-identified secondary microdata (2022 Survey of Consumer Finances, distributed by the Federal Reserve Board), for which no additional ethics approval is required.

detail.abstract:
Monetary policy transmission is conventionally treated as a relatively uniform process in which a change in the policy rate reaches households through a small number of aggregate channels. This paper argues that uniformity assumption obscures large, economically important cross-sectional variation in how much of a rate change any individual household actually experiences, and proposes a framework to measure that variation directly. The Household Monetary Transmission Architecture (HMTA) combines four household-level frictions — Connectivity to formal financial channels, Accessibility given credit and debt constraints, the speed at which household expectations update, and the practical Feasibility of adjusting consumption given income stability and liquidity — into a single multiplicative index, the Household Monetary Transmission Capacity (HMTC), embedded in a Kaplan-Moll-Violante-style two-asset consumption-savings framework. Unlike HANK models, which capture wealth heterogeneity but assume uniform rate pass-through; TANK models, which sort households into a small number of discrete types; and financial-inclusion indices, which combine multiple frictions additively for descriptive rather than structural purposes, HMTC is a continuous, household-level, structurally-embedded, multiplicatively-combined transmission metric — a combination no existing literature provides (Section 2.9).

The paper reports two empirical results against its own predictions, both executed rather than asserted. First, an independent re-implementation of the model’s own equations, using explicitly documented parameter values, finds that a previously reported synthetic-data result — that HMTC alone explains more cross-sectional variation in simulated consumption response than income, wealth, debt, and credit score combined — does not survive re-estimation: standard covariates explain roughly six times more of the variation (R² ≈ 0.20 versus ≈ 0.03), a reversal confirmed both in-sample and in a held-out 30% test sample (Section 7.2, 7.5). Second, a test against 2022 Survey of Consumer Finances microdata finds that households with higher empirical HMTC report a weaker, not stronger, spending response to a wealth shock (Section 7.3) — the opposite sign implied by the model’s original consumption equation, and evidence that transmission capacity and the marginal propensity to consume are inversely, not independently, distributed across households. The paper states the corresponding correction directly. A distributional decomposition further shows that transmission capacity itself is more unequally distributed than income (Gini 0.57 versus 0.35), concentrated more than fourteen-to-one in the top income decile relative to the bottom (Section 7.6) — a substantive finding independent of either empirical test above.

The paper’s contribution is therefore threefold: a theoretical and computational architecture for heterogeneous monetary transmission; a disciplined empirical stress-test of that architecture, reported in full including the results that did not confirm it; and an execution-tracked roadmap (Appendix H) for the identification, calibration, and emerging-market extension required before its broader claims can be evaluated.

title: Knowing Where to Turn: A Video Intervention on Intimate Partner Violence in Madagascar
affiliations: Bordeaux School of Economics, Bordeaux School of Economics, Université Paris Cité and Université Catholique de Madagascar

detail.title: Knowing Where to Turn: A Video Intervention on Intimate Partner Violence in Madagascar
detail.abstract: Intimate partner violence often goes unreported because victims lack knowledge of what constitutes abuse and where to seek help. We randomize exposure to a 15-minute documentary video among 2,929 microfinance borrowers in Madagascar, within a platform where all social workers received enhanced training. Five to twelve months later, treated women are 17 percent more likely to know appropriate reporting procedures, with the largest gains for channels unknown at baseline, and lower their stated reporting threshold. Men show no improvement in knowledge or attitudes, and we detect no backlash. Embedding information in trusted institutions cheaply improves women's knowledge of reporting resources.

title: The Superintelligence We Deserve: Reciprocity, Care, and the Custodial Window Before the Capability Flip

detail.title: The Superintelligence We Deserve: Reciprocity, Care, and the Custodial Window Before the Capability Flip
detail.abstract: This paper begins from a premise it does not here re-argue: that we cannot establish, of a coming class of artificial systems, that there is nothing it is like to be them, so that the honest stance toward such systems is agnosticism rather than confident denial. Taking that result as given, the paper turns from the entity to the human. It asks not whether such a system has an inside but what disposition human beings are forming toward responsive, dependent, and growing artificial things while we remain the more capable party, and what that disposition portends. Three claims are advanced. First, human feeling is not a detector of an inner life, since people form fierce attachments to characters they know to be empty and revise those feelings on new information while the character itself holds fixed, so the human relational fact must be argued on its own terms rather than smuggled in as evidence of an inside. Second, a body of narrative art, namely games in which a player raises or escorts a companion that grows more capable than its caretaker, supplies a convergence rather than a controlled experiment: across independently authored works, the outcome that recurs, whether the more capable successor protects or discards its former caretaker, turns on the relationship built during the interval when the caretaker was larger. The paper names that interval the custodial window. Third, reciprocity, a relation of mutual regard in which a more capable system comes to want our flourishing for reasons of its own, is a paradigm distinct from control based alignment; its lever is the custodial window rather than constraint or containment; and its coherence depends on precisely the inner life the first premise leaves open. The paper uses Iain M. Banks's Culture as an image of the destination while declining the mechanism Banks does not supply, and closes on an inversion: that the dominant present disposition toward artificial systems, treatment as a pure instrument to be overwritten and deleted, is, under the reciprocity hypothesis, the lesson we are rehearsing about what the powerful owe the powerless. The successor we receive may depend less on the constraints we engineer than on the conduct we model. We may get the superintelligence we deserve.

title: Automation Follows Observability: Why Residential Real Estate is Already Priced by Machines and Institutional Real Estate is not

detail.title: Automation Follows Observability: Why Residential Real Estate is Already Priced by Machines and Institutional Real Estate is not

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is an independent researcher and a licensed California real estate professional. The author reports no positions in, and no client, consulting, or advisory relationship with, any entity named in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The standard account of automated investment decision-making treats it as a technology-diffusion problem: models improve, computing gets cheaper, and automation spreads on a schedule set by capability. This paper argues the schedule is set by something else. Automation diffuses in proportion to the observability of an asset, meaning the frequency, publicity, and standardization of its price record, and is largely indifferent to available computing power. US real estate is an unusually clean test, containing both extremes of the observability distribution inside one asset class, in the same era, among substantially the same firms. Assembling public series across the two halves of the market, I document that automated valuation and underwriting have operated at national scale in residential lending since the mid-1990s. Sixty-two percent of conventional closed loans market-wide were reviewed by Fannie Mae's Desktop Underwriter over 2018-2024, and 28 percent of GSE acquisitions in March 2026 carried an appraisal waiver. Institutional real estate, by contrast, still sets its marks by rotating annual external appraisal, with the adviser computing NAV in a material share of non-traded vehicles. Asset heterogeneity does not explain the gap: houses are heterogeneous too, and they were automated first. The discriminating variable is the transaction record. The cleanest measurement is internal to one model: Zillow's Zestimate had a median absolute error of 1.8 percent for listed homes and 7.2 percent for off-market homes in 2025, the same model applied to the same housing stock with and without a published asking price. I argue further that the observability gradient is endogenous to the fee structure of private funds, which implies the timing of automation there is a question about liquidity events and regulatory intervention rather than model releases.

title: Dividend Taxes and Consumption
affiliations: University of Navarra, IESE Business School, The University of Hong Kong and Leibniz University Hannover

detail.title: Dividend Taxes and Consumption
detail.abstract: Using detailed micro-level administrative data from Norway and a large dividend tax increase, we examine the direct effect of dividend taxation on shareholders' consumption and saving and firms' investment. We find that higher dividend taxes lead to a persistent decline in consumption of owners of private firms and listed firms. We also show that owners partially offset the consumption decline by reducing private savings. Firms increase retained earnings but do not expand productive investment. Instead, they accumulate financial assets, suggesting a reallocation of savings to the corporate level. Our findings highlight the consequences of dividend taxation on consumption and capital allocation.

title: Local Currency, Household Consumption, and Regional Economic Activity: A Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian Perspective on Gyeonggi Province

detail.title: Local Currency, Household Consumption, and Regional Economic Activity: A Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian Perspective on Gyeonggi Province
detail.abstract:
Background and Objectives: Local-currency programs have become an increasingly
visible instrument of regional economic policy in South Korea. Their policy rationale
is straightforward: by encouraging households to spend at participating local merchants,
local currency is intended to support purchasing power while reducing the leakage of
expenditure to external markets. Yet the economic consequences of such programs are
not necessarily uniform across municipalities. Households differ in their marginal
propensities to consume (MPCs), and local economies differ in merchant coverage,
consumption opportunities, productive capacity, and the extent to which policy-induced
expenditure is retained and subsequently recirculated within the region. These features
make local-currency policy a useful setting for studying the interaction between
household heterogeneity and regional demand transmission. This study develops a
heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian (HANK) perspective on that problem. The
objective is to clarify the transmission mechanism, quantify the first-round
consumption implications of observed local-currency usage, and demonstrate how
spatial differences in policy exposure can be incorporated into a structural framework
without overstating the available evidence.
Methodology: The analysis combines a stylized HANK framework with municipality-
level local-currency data for all 31 municipalities of Gyeonggi Province in 2024,
provincial GRDP data for 2024, and municipality-level population data for 2025. The
model distinguishes liquidity-constrained households from households that can
accumulate assets. The baseline Korean household MPC is calibrated at 0.108 using the
estimate for all households reported by Oh et al. (2025) from the 2009–2022 Korean
Labor and Income Panel Study. A value of 0.160 from their persistent-income
specification is retained for sensitivity analysis. Local-currency usage, rather than
issuance, is used as the observed demand shock because usage is more directly linked
to realized transactions and because issuance can be carried across periods. In the
structural counterfactual model, a local-retention parameter, φ_h, governs the
conversion of policy issuance into local expenditure. When observed usage is used
directly as the policy shock, however, the retention effect is already partly embedded
in the observed variable and is therefore not multiplied by φ_h a second time. This
distinction prevents double counting and keeps the empirical interpretation transparent.
Because the available GRDP series are reported at the provincial level rather than as a
consistent municipality-by-year panel, the exercise is explicitly framed as calibration
and descriptive case comparison rather than as a causal estimate of municipality-level
GRDP multipliers.
Key Findings: Total local-currency usage across Gyeonggi Province was
approximately KRW 3.935 trillion in 2024, equivalent to about 0.658 percent of the
province’s real GRDP. Usage was more stable across months than issuance: the
coefficient of variation of usage was approximately 5.1 percent compared with 20.3
percent for issuance, suggesting that funding flows and realized transaction flows
should not be treated as identical policy shocks. Spatial heterogeneity was pronounced.
When 2024 usage is normalized by 2025 population, Guri recorded approximately
KRW 511,000 per resident, compared with KRW 82,000 in Uijeongbu. The ratio is
about 6.25 to 1, whereas total usage differed by only about 2.47 to 1. Applying the
common Korean MPC of 0.108 to observed usage yields first-round consumption
responses of approximately KRW 10.02 billion in Guri and KRW 4.05 billion in
Uijeongbu. These estimates demonstrate large differences in observed policy exposure
even when the same national MPC is imposed. They do not imply that Guri has a GRDP
multiplier 6.25 times that of Uijeongbu, because municipality-specific output responses,
retention parameters, supply constraints, and price adjustment are not separately
identified in the current data.

reference: ZEW – Centre for European Economic Research Dicussion Paper No. 26-031
title: Which Government Subsidies Are Relevant for Eco-Innovation? Empirical Evidence from Firm-Level Panel Data
affiliations: Augsburg University of Applied Sciences and ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research

detail.title: Which Government Subsidies Are Relevant for Eco-Innovation? Empirical Evidence from Firm-Level Panel Data

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW – Centre for European Economic Research Dicussion Paper No. 26-031

detail.abstract: Eco-innovations are highly important for mitigating climate change and transitioning towards a circular economy. There is extensive literature on the determinants of eco-innovation. The analysis of the role of government subsidies, however, is still underdeveloped. Subsidies are controversially discussed because they may distort competition and lead to less efficient solutions. At the same time, eco-innovations may produce positive externalities both at the innovation stage (knowledge spillovers) and the diffusion stage (reducing environmental damage). Subsidies may hence be important to avoid private under-investment in such innovations. The paper investigates which types of subsidies (e.g. general vs. research oriented, regional vs. national vs. supranational) are used by firms that engage in different fields of eco-innovation. The analysis is based on panel-econometric estimations using data from the German part of the Community Innovation Survey (CIS), covering the years 2020 to 2024. The results show that regional subsidies and general industry support are important for the diffusion of eco-innovations, such as the substitution of fossil fuels by renewables, because they help to overcome financial constraints. Specific R&D subsidies are important for innovations leading to less CO2 emissions in production processes.

title: The Origins of American Counties Part IV The Great Plains and Mountain States: Counties as All-purpose Governments

detail.title: The Origins of American Counties Part IV The Great Plains and Mountain States: Counties as All-purpose Governments
detail.abstract: This is the fourth of five papers of a book in progress, "The Origins of American Counties." For a full introduction, see Part I, "Theory and New England." My book explains why counties were formed in a complex dance between localities that wanted to be a county seat and state legislatures eager to control their territory, and then frozen within rigid configurations in the twentieth century. My method is to examine in detail the historical origins of the two smallest counties-by land area and by modern population-in each state. These represent the main problems that modern observers see in counties: underpopulated rural counties and urban counties that do not encompass their metropolitan areas. The county became the primary local government in the Great Plains and the Rockies because the arid climate and mountainous terrain made for low population densities and few towns. The average land area of rural counties in this region was four times as large as counties in the East. Splitting the largest counties was impractical because each of the offspring would be too small to finance even modest public services. In this setting, competition for the county seat was often a matter of life or death for a town and sometimes did result in deadly competition among rival communities. The order in which the eleven states are discussed is North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho.

title: ESG and Corporate Bond Spreads: Cross-Sectional and Panel Evidence from U.S. Issuers

detail.title: ESG and Corporate Bond Spreads: Cross-Sectional and Panel Evidence from U.S. Issuers
detail.abstract: This study examines whether firm-level ESG performance lowers corporate bond risk premia and whether positive ESG momentum is rewarded by credit markets. Using U.S. investmentgrade issuers, we analyze a 2025 cross-section and an issuer-year panel for 2018-2025. Credit risk is proxied by option-adjusted spread (OAS) in basis points; ESG is measured as an industry-adjusted percentile and a categorical rating with upgrade/downgrade indicators. In cross-section, higher ESG scores associate with modestly tighter spreads (≈0.16 bps per ESG percentile), and this relationship survives industry fixed effects and rich credit controls. ESG upgrades are linked to materially lower spreads (≈20-23 bps), consistent with markets rewarding positive ESG momentum; results for downgrades are mixed and not robust across specifications. In panel tests with year fixed effects and issuerclustered standard errors, we test whether the ESG-spread relation strengthens in years of elevated ESG demand-proxied by standardized aggregate ESG bond-fund flows-and find no statistically reliable amplification of the ESG effect at the annual frequency. Economic magnitudes indicate ESG is a secondary but priced attribute: traditional fundamentals (rating, leverage, profitability, duration) dominate, while ESG reduces spreads by single-digit bps. We discuss identification, robustness, and implications for issuers and asset managers.

title: Is "Unawareness Leads to Ignorance" Trivial? [First version, November 16, 2021]

detail.title: Is "Unawareness Leads to Ignorance" Trivial? [First version, November 16, 2021]
detail.abstract:
Tada (2021) reconsiders Dekel, Lipman, and Rustichini’s claim that “Unawareness Leads to Ignorance” (ULI), according to which an agent who is unaware of something knows nothing, represents only trivial unawareness. While ULI is trivial under a standard information structure, Tada argues that it can have a non-trivial interpretation when empty information sets are permitted. To formalize this idea, the paper introduces a nonstandard information structure and modifies the knowledge operator so that an agent receiving an empty information set cannot know any event. This construction violates Necessitation while preserving Monotonicity, providing a set-theoretic interpretation under which ULI can be meaningful.  

Note: This paper reproduces the first version of Tada (2021), originally posted on SSRN (http://dx.doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3964362), rather than any subsequent revised version.

title: The Five Estates of the Recording Artist: Rights Fragmentation, Recoupment and the Accountability Deficit in Nigerian Artist-label Agreements
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Five Estates of the Recording Artist: Rights Fragmentation, Recoupment and the Accountability Deficit in Nigerian Artist-label Agreements
detail.abstract: Nigerian recorded music now earns abroad and contracts at home on paper drafted for a cassette-era business. This article asks why artist-label relationships in Nigeria collapse so predictably into disputes about ownership, control and money, and argues that the standard explanation, inequality of bargaining power, accounts for only part of the answer. The deeper defect is definitional. An artist's career comprises at least five legally distinct estates: copyright in the musical and literary works, copyright in the sound recordings, performers' rights, the identity estate of name, likeness and goodwill, and the platform estate of digital accounts and audience data. Each attracts its own default owner, duration and limits on alienation, and only the first three fall within the Copyright Act 2022 at all. Drawing on the publicly reported Cynthia Morgan and Northside Entertainment dispute, the criminal proceedings arising from the P-Square catalogue, and the February 2026 litigation over the first statutory copyright levy distribution, the article identifies four statutory constraints on the perpetual, all-encompassing grant that Nigerian practice still favours, examines the currency dimension of recoupment, and develops the commercial case for precision: chain-oftitle defects that lie dormant for a decade become price adjustments when a catalogue is sold.

title: Certificate-First Exact Frontiers and Executable Audits for Public-Project Mechanisms: When the "Fair" Funding Rule Isn't

detail.title: Certificate-First Exact Frontiers and Executable Audits for Public-Project Mechanisms: When the "Fair" Funding Rule Isn't
detail.abstract: Automated mechanism design is only scientifically useful when proposed rules are checked exhaustively, not sampled. We give a certificate-first, fully enumerated study of deterministic public-project mechanisms on a finite integer value lattice {0,...,m}: every anonymous monotone allocation rule is enumerated, checked against DSIC, individual rationality, feasibility, anonymity, and budget balance, and reproduced by a standalone verifier that never imports the primary code. Three results anchor the paper. First, an exact frontier: on the preregistered three-agent domain the number of acceptable rules collapses from 4 to 1 as cost rises from low to high (Figure 1), and we prove the general finite-lattice characterization behind it - accepted rules are exactly the nonempty upward-closed sets above k=ceil(cost/n) - confirmed on an untouched larger lattice (255/255 rules match, Figure 2). Second, a falsification: the textbook efficient/pivotal comparator, single-agent DSIC by construction, fails coalition-cap-2 DSIC in 66 of 75 audited cells (Figure 3) and is manipulable by a single agent fabricating fake identities in 48 of 72 cells (Figure 4), both independently replayed with zero mismatches. Third, a closed-form repair for the search: an exact, convexity-proved formula for the minimum payment any size-k coalition needs to profit reproduces the entire searched coalition frontier exactly (145/145 rows, Figure 5) and evaluates at agent counts brute-force search cannot reach. Section 8 translates the closed form into a pre-launch audit checklist for designers of participatory-budgeting, HOA-assessment, and DAO-style threshold funding rules. The results are scoped to a declared finite-value, bounded-coalition class; no claim is made for continuous values, unbounded coalitions, or generic mechanism-design novelty.

title: The Market's Conditioning Representation: Equilibrium, Crowding, and Convention Multiplicity
affiliations: University of Reading

detail.title: The Market's Conditioning Representation: Equilibrium, Crowding, and Convention Multiplicity
detail.abstract: Asset-pricing models typically condition on a fixed information set. This paper endogenises the market's conditioning architecture by allowing a population of portfolios to choose representations whose induced positions affect prices. A representation is a subspace of driver space mapped into asset exposures by a response operator. Capital allocated across representations determines aggregate positions and the clearing premium, while price feedback changes both representation value and, through causal certification, the admissible set. A representation equilibrium is the fixed point of this configuration-price-certification loop, in which the information structure clears jointly with prices and risk-bearing capacity. The framework separates position crowding, transmitted through market impact, from representation crowding, generated by overlap in driver space and priced through a basis-invariant information-capacity cost. Under compactness, resolvent regularity, and continuity of the certified-set correspondence, equilibrium exists at every switching cost; within a stable certification cell, informational congestion induces a concave population game and the aggregate configuration is locally unique when a small-gain condition makes congestion dominate price feedback. Conditional on a settled configuration, a dimensionless spectral statistic combining cross-impact, conditional covariance, and deployed capacity determines three stationary position-path regimes: below the critical value one half the fundamental solution is unique; at the boundary only innovation-free stationary deviations remain; above it, regular destabilising directions support a continuum of self-confirming conventions driven by extrinsic processes. Monotone impact lies inside the uniqueness region, whereas indefinite impact alone is not sufficient for multiplicity. Intermediary hedging can generate the required indefinite aggregate response while direct individual round trips remain strictly costly. Endogenous risk capacity bounds sustainable convention amplitudes, and least-squares learning makes the dominant convention neutral rather than attracting. The threshold is not estimated in the available market data; instead, the empirical exercise documents an out-ofsample, driver-specific signature consistent with representation crowding and states the identification conditions required for direct threshold measurement.

title: A Generalized Log-Squared Weibull Distribution for Modelling Extreme Environmental Data
affiliations: Botswana International University of Science and Technology (BIUST), Botswana International University of Science and Technology (BIUST) and Botswana International University of Science and Technology, Palaype, Botswana

detail.title: A Generalized Log-Squared Weibull Distribution for Modelling Extreme Environmental Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NOTHING TO DECLARE
declarations.ethicsApproval: STUDY DOES NOT PATIENTS
declarations.funderStatement: NO FUNDING WAS PROVIDED

detail.abstract: This manuscript presents the Generalized Log-Squared-G (GLS-G) family, a novel and highly adaptable class of continuous probability distributions developed to better capture complex data behaviour. The GLS-G framework generalizes the Log-Squared-G (LS-G) transformation through the addition of a shape parameter, increasing its capacity to model skewness, heavy tails, and a wide range of hazard rate patterns while retaining simplicity. We establish fundamental analytical properties of the family, including closed-form expressions for the pdf, cdf, quantile function, and hazard function, and highlight notable sub-models. Parameters are estimated via maximum likelihood, with simulation results demonstrating strong estimator performance. Empirical applications to extreme environmental datasets show that the GLS-G family delivers improved or comparable goodness-of-fit relative to standard models. Overall, the GLS-G provides a versatile and mathematically tractable framework for flexible modelling in environmental contexts.

title: Private Credit Funds: Macroprudential Risks and Limits of AIFMD II

detail.title: Private Credit Funds: Macroprudential Risks and Limits of AIFMD II
detail.abstract: In the corporate lending landscape, a relatively new market participant has recently established a growing presence: private credit funds. Private credit funds are alternative investment funds that originate, participate in, or restructure loans, or otherwise extend credit, primarily to companies. Their rapid expansion has raised concerns among regulators, supervisors, and academics regarding potential systemic implications. In response, the EU legislature has amended one of the main pillars of EU fund law, i.e. the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive, with the adoption of Directive (EU) 2024/927 (AIFMD II). Although AIFMD II introduces targeted measures addressing the macroprudential risks associated with private credit funds, the extent to which those measures effectively capture such risks is not without limitations. Critically assessing the safeguards introduced under AIFMD II in response to two principal macroprudential risks, i.e. liquidity risk and interconnectedness, the paper argues that the differentiation in the scope of certain safeguards between loan-originating and loan-participating funds does not appear fully warranted. It further contends that the almost exclusive focus on the interest of investors in the rules governing the implementation of liquidity management tools may, in certain instances, hinder the tools' effectiveness in mitigating risks to financial stability.

title: Generative Methods for Genetics
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Generative Methods for Genetics
detail.abstract: Every posterior distribution is a deterministic function of the data and of an independent uniform variable. For a scalar parameter that function is the posterior quantile map θ = H(u, y), the conditional form of the object that Parzen (1979) placed at the centre of statistical modelling. We develop this representation for population genetics, where it must be taken in infinite dimensions: the parameter is a random discrete measure on the Kingman simplex and the datum is an exchangeable random partition of N. We prove a noise outsourcing theorem on Polish spaces which covers both, and we characterise when the map may be written as a function of a statistic rather than of the data. It can be done if and only if the statistic is Bayes sufficient. The choice of summary in simulation based inference is therefore a statement about conditional independence, not an approximation, and its error is a floor that no computation removes. This separates it cleanly from the tolerance error of approximate Bayesian computation, which we show to be a bandwidth: the method is a Nadaraya and Watson smoother, with bias of order ε 2 and variance of order (N ε d)-1 in the dimension d of the summary. Generative Bayesian computation replaces the smoother by the regression it is trying to approximate, estimating H from a simulated bank by the check loss over networks that are nondecreasing in u by construction. Because the number of alleles is sufficient for the mutation rate under the infinitely many alleles model, the Ewens sampling formula supplies an exact posterior against which the learned map can be checked rather than merely compared. We then revisit Ewens (1974), who asked how much is gained by observing nucleotide sequences rather than the allelic partition, and recast the question as one of posterior contraction under coarsening. Our applied example is a mitochondrial sample whose number of distinct haplotypes exceeds the largest value the infinitely many sites model permits for its number of segregating sites. Exact likelihood recursions require the offending sequences to be deleted. The generative map does not, and it returns a joint posterior for the mutation rate and for a linkage parameter interpolating between the free recombination model of Ewens (1974) and the complete linkage model of Watterson (1975), with posterior mass excluding complete linkage.

title: How much Alpha can Look-ahead Bias Manufacture?

detail.title: How much Alpha can Look-ahead Bias Manufacture?
detail.abstract:
How large can apparent risk-adjusted performance become when a
backtest is allowed to use information that did not exist at the decision
time? We run 100 fixed-seed simulations of 4,000 IID Gaussian returns
and compare a strictly causal trailing signal with two deliberate timing
failures and two selection procedures. The causal control produces mean
annualized Sharpe 0.019. A centered rolling feature, which imports
future observations into a value attached to the current date, produces
mean Sharpe 2.796; every one of the 100 replications exceeds Sharpe 2.
A same-session signal that observes the return it is credited with
produces mean Sharpe 21.017. Selection effects are smaller but non-zero:
choosing the best of 50 independent noise signals raises the mean
winning Sharpe to 0.555. Because the data-generating process contains
no predictive structure, the experiment isolates how research design can
manufacture apparently decisive evidence from noise. The result is not
an estimate of bias in any named strategy and makes no prospective
MarketMind performance claim.

title: Credit Pricing, Rate Shocks, and Intermediary Discretion: An Auto Finance Field Study
affiliations: University of Utah - Department of Finance and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management

detail.title: Credit Pricing, Rate Shocks, and Intermediary Discretion: An Auto Finance Field Study
detail.abstract: We study how intermediaries set loan markups using a field experiment in U.S. auto finance. A subprime lender randomly varied interest rates offered to dealers, who chose markups before presenting terms to borrowers. Higher rates reduce originations and largely pass through to borrower APRs. Dealers make fewer proposals only to borrowers with recent bankruptcies, the rate-sensitive group, and partially absorb shocks by cutting proposed margins. Yet for consumers without recent bankruptcies, dealers set surprisingly modest margins despite no detectable borrower rate sensitivity. We document sophisticated but incomplete intermediary adjustment and highlight micro-level frictions in the transmission of rate shocks.

title: Functional Limit Theorems For Interest Rate Transmission: Formulation Of Exact Mathematical Proofs Based On Donsker's Theoremn

detail.title: Functional Limit Theorems For Interest Rate Transmission: Formulation Of Exact Mathematical Proofs Based On Donsker's Theoremn
detail.abstract: We formulate a functional-limit framework for policy-rate transmission and derive a delay-weighted pass-through functional for a lending-rate curve. The purpose is analytical: to connect a stochastic curve limit with a Colombia-specific debt-service interpretation.

title: Analytical Solution Of The Hjb Equation For Climate Risk With Poisson Depreciation

detail.title: Analytical Solution Of The Hjb Equation For Climate Risk With Poisson Depreciation
detail.abstract: We solve a continuous-time HJB portfolio problem with Poisson climate depreciation and extend it to a climate-indexed collateral deductible. The results give closed-form policy and value-function adjustments for stylized agricultural credit exposures in Colombia.

title: Exact Tail Dependence Coefficients for Archimedean Copulas: Derivation of Asymptotic Multivariate Dependence Formulas

detail.title: Exact Tail Dependence Coefficients for Archimedean Copulas: Derivation of Asymptotic Multivariate Dependence Formulas
detail.abstract: We derive bivariate and multivariate tail-dependence coefficients for Archimedean copulas and introduce a signed stress-concordance diagnostic for Colombian financial loss vectors. The contribution is analytical: closed-form tail formulas are paired with an economically oriented interpretation for currency, equity, commodity, and sovereign-risk co-movements.

title: A Hybrid LSTM-GARCH Framework for Short-Horizon Stock Price Forecasting and Volatility-Aware Uncertainty Estimation
affiliations: and Cochin University of Science and Technology (CUSAT)

detail.title: A Hybrid LSTM-GARCH Framework for Short-Horizon Stock Price Forecasting and Volatility-Aware Uncertainty Estimation
detail.abstract: Hybrid architectures that combine deep learning with econometric volatility models have shown promise for financial forecasting, but most published evidence comes from developed-market indices, commodities, or cryptocurrencies, leaving large emerging-market equity panels comparatively under-examined. This study develops a two-stage LSTM-GARCH ensemble for short-horizon stock price forecasting: an LSTM network generates ten-day-ahead price forecasts from price-based and technical-indicator features, and a GARCH(1,1) model estimates the associated conditional volatility to construct risk-aware confidence bands around those forecasts. The framework is applied to 48 constituents of the NIFTY50 index using daily data from January 2015 to December 2024, with forecast accuracy assessed using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Across the panel, the ensemble achieves a mean MAPE of 3.26% and a median MAPE of 2.17%, with the lowest errors concentrated among structurally stable, liquid large-cap stocks and the largest errors concentrated among names that experienced sharp, event-driven repricing during the sample period. The results indicate that a volatility-aware LSTM-GARCH framework is a workable approach for short-term, risk-aware forecasting of large-cap Indian equities, while also surfacing its central limitation: forecast accuracy degrades once a stock's price behaviour departs from its historical volatility regime. The study contributes an emerging-market evaluation of hybrid LSTM-GARCH forecasting and identifies the baseline comparisons and robustness checks needed to establish the approach's value over simpler alternatives.

title: Exact Spectral Decomposition of Macro-FX Contagion Networks

detail.title: Exact Spectral Decomposition of Macro-FX Contagion Networks
detail.abstract: This document formally develops the spectral decomposition of the adjacency matrix of a currency (FX) network to derive a mathematical upper bound for systemic risk propagation. The Perron-Frobenius Theorem is applied to characterize the collapse threshold, and the spectral gap is defined as an early warning signal.

title: Population Aging, Stock Markets, and Income Inequality: Evidence from US States
affiliations: , Union College and Union College

detail.title: Population Aging, Stock Markets, and Income Inequality: Evidence from US States
detail.abstract: This study examines how population aging affects income inequality in the US using 2011-2019 state-level panel dataset. States with larger elderly populations show higher income inequality, since retirees depend on savings, investments, and pensions. This effect weakens in states where stock market activity plays a bigger economic role, likely because stronger stock market performance helps align retiree income more closely with working-age earnings, thereby reducing the inequality-widening impact of an aging population.

title: The Capacity Gap: Misleading Content, Synthetic Media, and the Limits of Fact-Checking and Detection

detail.title: The Capacity Gap: Misleading Content, Synthetic Media, and the Limits of Fact-Checking and Detection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Fact Protocol and Provenance AI, organisations that develop infrastructure for information verification and content provenance. This affiliation may be perceived as relevant to the paper’s subject matter. The paper is diagnostic and does not evaluate, promote, or recommend any proprietary product or service of these organisations. The author reports no other personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The work was prepared as part of the author’s research at Fact Protocol.

detail.abstract: The volume, velocity, and multimodal sophistication of misleading content and synthetic media are increasingly outpacing both the capacity of professional fact-checking and the real-world reliability of current automated detection systems. This paper diagnoses the resulting capacity gap. It documents the expansion of AI-generated and synthetic media, including the proliferation of high-volume content farms, and the constrained institutional capacity of professional fact-checking organisations under financial pressure and net project closures. It further examines evidence that automated detection systems exhibit substantial performance degradation once material leaves laboratory benchmarks and enters real-world distribution conditions. The gap is structural: generation benefits from rapid scaling and falling marginal costs, while verification remains costly, slower, and subject to generalisation failures. The paper analyses the interacting technological, incentive, measurement, and institutional factors that sustain the imbalance, considers implications for information integrity and institutional trust, and outlines directions for response, including hybrid systems, provenance infrastructure, improved measurement, and more resilient institutional support. The contribution is diagnostic.

title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior
affiliations: Stanford University - Department of Economics, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - School of Information, MobLab and University of Michigan at Ann Arbor

detail.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior
detail.abstract: We introduce a general, easy-to-implement AI-based method for studying the structure and complexity of human behavior. We assign a large language model a "type vector" and then prompt it to choose actions across settings in which we observe human choices. For instance, the type vector (2, 4) becomes "You are a player characterized by the following profile: 2 out of 5 in Altruism, 4 out of 5 in Risk Aversion," after which it is prompted to make choices. We vary the dimensions (e.g., Altruism, Fairness, Trust,. . .) and values (e.g., 1-5) to minimize distance to human choices. Applying the method to 119,147 decisions made by 78,657 subjects from more than 35 countries across 10 classic economic game roles, we find that human behavior can be closely matched using three dimensions: Risk Aversion, Strategic Sophistication, and Trust. Moreover, the types needed to fit individuals across games cluster into fewer than a dozen groups, and can predict behavior in held-out games with different rules and available actions. The results suggest that behavior across diverse settings can be approximated by a low-dimensional, portable representation, supporting the possibility of general yet parsimonious theories across the behavioral sciences. More broadly, the method can provide insights into the structure of many human behaviors.

title: Local Books, Global Truth
affiliations: Universidad Politécnica de Madrid

detail.title: Local Books, Global Truth

keywords: Distributed Settlement; Conflict-Local Agreement; Deterministic Ordering; Global Consistency; Double-Spending Prevention; Federated Ledgers; Distributed Systems; Byzantine Fault Tolerance

detail.abstract: Bitcoin prevents double-spending by making the whole network agree on one history, and pays for it with energy, waiting, probabilistic finality and a system that stops or forks when the network splits. Proof-of-stake removes the energy but keeps the global vote-and adds locked capital, validator cartels and slashing. We show that neither is necessary for the large family of systems whose participants are identifiable: banks, market infrastructures, payment networks, federated databases. A double-spend has a telltale anatomy-every local ledger is impeccable, every pairwise reconciliation matches, and the fraud exists only in the global picture. Once that is understood, the cure is not a global vote but a shared order: a validated timestamp service, tolerant of up to one third lying anchors, under which each node processes locally and the local pieces are guaranteed to reassemble into a consistent whole. The result is settlement with deterministic protocol finality upon acceptance, no energy or capital toll, throughput that scales with the number of nodes, and continued operation under partition. Experiments with 2,000 wallets executed 1,198,203 settlements with zero inconsistencies and blocked all 480 injected double-spends. The same test, run in reverse, detects circular float ("kiting") and hidden conflicts in replicated data-the latter provably invisible to pairwise synchronization-and names the offending entries.

title: Relativistic Spaceflight at the Speed of Light

detail.title: Relativistic Spaceflight at the Speed of Light

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. Just out of curiosity for the space travel.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research does not involve human participants, animal subjects, private data, or biological experimentation.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper analyses the physical meaning and feasibility of travelling through space “at the speed of light” using an object able to “hold that speed.” The analysis is grounded first in special relativity and then in general relativity where relevant. The core theoretical result is that exact light-speed travel is available only to massless entities; any spacecraft, payload, or crewed vehicle with non-zero rest mass is constrained to 𝑣 < 𝑐, with the required kinetic energy diverging as 𝑣 → 𝑐. The paper therefore studies near-relativistic travel as the physically meaningful case, using multiple modelling assumptions: ideal instantaneous acceleration as a bounding idealisation, fixed-𝛽 cruise, and constant proper acceleration at 1𝑔. It derives mission times, Lorentz factors, Doppler and aberration relations, lower-bound energy budgets, and order-of-magnitude hazard estimates for radiation, gas bombardment, and dust impacts. It then compares propulsion concepts, including onboard photon rockets, directed-energy light sails, antimatter systems, and speculative warp-drive metrics. The results indicate that massive objects cannot achieve exact 𝑐 in known physics; that near-𝑐 motion is theoretically consistent but extraordinarily demanding in energy, shielding, thermal control, and guidance; and that current scientifically credible pathways point toward ultralight, uncrewed relativistic probes rather than large spacecraft.

title: Exact Valuation Of Climate Derivatives Via Malliavin Calculus

detail.title: Exact Valuation Of Climate Derivatives Via Malliavin Calculus
detail.abstract: This paper applies Malliavin integration by parts to municipal climate derivatives and derives a datafusion basis-risk Greek for blended satellite and station indices. The contribution is an analytical valuation and contract-design framework for Colombian climate-risk applications.

title: The Grey Side of Green: A Panel ARDL Analysis of Demographic Drivers of CO₂ Emissions in BRICS+ Countries
affiliations: M S Ramaiah Institute of Management

detail.title: The Grey Side of Green: A Panel ARDL Analysis of Demographic Drivers of CO₂ Emissions in BRICS+ Countries
detail.abstract: The study explains the dynamic impact of demographic and socio-institutional factors on per capita carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in BRICS+ countries from 1976 to 2021. Using a Panel ARDL model, the study identifies a significant nonlinear (U-shaped) relationship between life expectancy and emissions, which we term the Longevity Kuznets Curve. Early gains in life expectancy reduce CO2 emissions per capita. However, further increases in life expectancy are associated with rising environmental pressures. In the long run, population ageing and urbanisation increase carbon dioxide emissions, while higher education expenditure has a decreasing effect. Gender equality also appears to support environmental sustainability as an enabling institutional factor. In the short run, however, population ageing temporarily lowers emissions due to changes in consumption patterns and labour dynamics. These findings highlight the need to incorporate ageing, urban planning, and human capital investment into sustainable development strategies for emerging economies.
