title: Common Shocks and the Measurement of Fragility in Financial Intermediaries

detail.title: Common Shocks and the Measurement of Fragility in Financial Intermediaries
detail.abstract: We examine how common asset-value shocks are reflected in the market-implied fragility of commercial banks and mortgage real estate investment trusts. A standard corporate default measure places banks far from default, but this largely reflects how the default barrier is built: it captures a median of about 3% of a bank's liabilities, because it omits deposits, but about 70% of these trusts'. On a barrier defined consistently from total liabilities, the apparent gap collapses, with the median distance-to-default difference falling from 6.6 units to 0.7, and both sectors deteriorate together during the 2020 and 2022-2023 shocks. Within banks, securities losses predict fragility only weakly, while pre-shock uninsured funding matters mainly during the acute March 2023 crisis.

title: Volatility Recovers before Network Structure: Structural Hysteresis in Global Equity Propagation Networks
affiliations: Independent Quantitative Researcher

detail.title: Volatility Recovers before Network Structure: Structural Hysteresis in Global Equity Propagation Networks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses publicly available financial market data and does not involve human participants, personal data, clinical subjects, or animal research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Do equity-market volatility networks return to their pre-shock state when observed volatility itself normalizes? This paper develops a past-information-only, multi-horizon operator representation of cross-sectional volatility propagation and uses it to distinguish scalar stress recovery from recovery of the propagation geometry. The evidence supports five empirical conclusions. Propagation geometry is often highly concentrated relative to the underlying equity dimension, although the degree of compression varies across markets. Horizon loadings are systematically horizon-dependent, but the data do not support a universal monotone-decay law. Volatility shocks generate positive geometric deformation in multiple locked-confirmatory markets. After scalar stress returns to its normal regime, a positive structural gap remains, and structural half-recovery is frequently right-censored through 504 trading sessions while volatility half-recovery is finite. A complementary proposition shows that, for a clockwise-oriented stress-distance loop, matched-stress recovery above the loading branch implies a strictly positive structural loop area. The contribution is therefore a recovery result: volatility normalization and network restoration are distinct empirical objects.

title: Economic Valuation of Urban Greenspace in Public Damage Assessment Context: Integrated Financial Modelling for the City of Moscow
affiliations: Moscow State University, Westminster International University in Tashkent (WIUT) and The State University of Management - Department of Economic measurements

detail.title: Economic Valuation of Urban Greenspace in Public Damage Assessment Context: Integrated Financial Modelling for the City of Moscow
detail.abstract: In many countries of the world, ecosystem services, i.e. economic benefits provided by greenspace, are indispensable public amenities taken into consideration when valuing greenspaces. This study, commissioned in the context of developing Guidelines for valuation of damages to greenspaces in the city of Moscow, presents a comprehensive methodology for valuation of greenspaces that integrates the replacement cost valuation basis for damaged green areas with accounting for an array of key ecosystem functions performed by greenspace, such as: ambient temperature reduction, PM2.5 and PM10 dust absorption, biodiversity, CO2 sequestration, water drainage, and provision of aesthetic services. Thus, the value of urban plant life, including trees, shrubbery and lawns, was assessed by three components: the initial (capital) costs of purchasing, transporting and planting trees; capitalized costs of annual care; and the capitalized value of ecosystem services provided by greenspace. The proposed methodology relies on a combination of the replacement cost and benefits-based ecosystem service valuation approaches –as applied to the developed matrix of sui generis plant-life classification made up of 7 specie-wise groupings by 5 green-space spatial configurations (courtyards; streets and highways; parks and gardens; Greened squares, boulevards, embankments; forest areas) -- helping to account for the variability of ecosystem service provision in a most balanced, userfriendly way. To incorporate into the valuation process the demand aspect for ecosystem services provided by greenspace, we also delineate three assessment zones in our analysis, conforming to the radial spatial organization of Moscow. Our findings indicate that the total economic value of an individual mature tree varies from USD 5000 to USD 25000, depending on the assessment zone, specie-wise classification and spatial configuration in which the tree is found to be growing, as well as having regard to all the key ecosystem services, except for the provision of the aesthetic function. It is also estimated that the share of ecosystem services in the total assessed value of greenspace varies from 30-60% in urban landscape settings to 95% in the forested zones of the New Moscow.

title:
Meeting Halfway: 
Inequality Aversion and Mutual Compromise
affiliations: Nankai University - School of Economics and School of Economics, Nankai University

detail.title:
Meeting Halfway: 
Inequality Aversion and Mutual Compromise
detail.abstract: Individuals hold diverse ideals. Whether they form social connections despite these differences-and thereby achieve social cohesion-depends on tolerance (how much difference one is willing to accept) and compromise (a choice to adjust one's position toward the other). Standard theory predicts that only the more tolerant party ever compromises, and only minimally. This implies that to induce cohesion, extremists must be far more tolerant than moderates (Genicot, 2022). We introduce inequality aversion into this framework and show, both theoretically and experimentally, that mutual high compromise can be sustained as a welfare-improving equilibrium. This equilibrium emerges most readily when tolerance levels are similar and agents choose whether to connect after observing each other's compromises (73% high compromise in our experiment under these conditions). Our analysis thus identifies fairness concerns as an additional mechanism sustaining cohesion, one that, unlike the standard mechanism, operates more effectively among individuals with similar tolerance.

title: Towards a Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence: A Framework for Studying the Institutional, Geopolitical, Technological-Material, Socio-Democratic, and Ecological Layers
affiliations: University of Algarve and

detail.title: Towards a Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence: A Framework for Studying the Institutional, Geopolitical, Technological-Material, Socio-Democratic, and Ecological Layers

contentType.other: Article initial version, to be published in a journal or as a book chapter

detail.abstract: The rise of artificial intelligence marks a turning point with consequences that reach deep into politics, ecology, and even the future of civilization. AI is much more than a mere set of technologies. It has become a kind of critical infrastructure and, at the same time, a regime of power capable of shaping norms and producing real-world effects. In doing so, it is quietly reshuffling the relationships between knowledge, production, power, and the socio-ecological metabolism that sustains modern life. This article approaches AI as an emerging institution, one that is taking shape within, and helping to redefine, technodigital capitalism. The method is deliberately essayistic and analytical-conceptual, weaving together insights from political economy, the social study of technology, political ecology, and institutional theory. Special attention is paid to what all of this means for the European Union and for the broader political economy of the twenty-first century. The argument put forward is a cautiously optimistic. If placed within the right public and democratic frameworks, AI could become a powerful ally for social innovation, helping to soften the impacts of the Anthropocene and to support strategies for more sustainable forms of growth.

title: Certified Tolerance: First-Order Welfare in a New Keynesian Model

detail.title: Certified Tolerance: First-Order Welfare in a New Keynesian Model
detail.abstract: Which simple rule should a central bank run in an economy that carries a wage commons, the microfounded demand externality by which atomistic wage suppression holds the labor share below the firms' own collective standard? This paper ranks three implementable rules in that economy, taken from the companion paper that derives it: a standard Taylor rule; the same rule with a tolerance clause that suspends the inflation response when a certificate shows wage-led recovery of the labor share below a stated ceiling; and a naive variant that suspends on wage inflation alone, without the certificate. The criterion is a stated welfare accounting: a level term computed per household type to first order around the distorted steady state, and a variance term, the standard quadratic loss, common to both types by assumption. Type welfare is aggregated with a stated Pareto weight on workers; the deliverable is a ranking as a function of that weight, never a claimed optimum. Three results. First, the ranking is regime-dependent by construction: at capacity, or absent any selection margin, the certified clause never fires, the tolerance rule coincides with the Taylor rule state by state, and the verdict of the monopsony sticky-price literature, stabilize inflation, is recovered as the boundary case. Second, in the demand-constrained regime the tolerance rule dominates the Taylor rule for all Pareto weights above a computed threshold; when the workers' spending propensity plus the induced-expenditure response exceeds one, the threshold is negative and the dominance holds even under capitalist-only weights. Third, the dominance is carried by a first-order selection term, the movement of the labor share along the ranked equilibrium continuum that the clause permits and the Taylor rule suppresses; at the calibration the stabilization cost of the clause is four orders of magnitude smaller than the selection gain, so the ranking is not a variance horse race and a rule evaluation that omits the selection margin gets the sign wrong where the escape path operates. The certificate itself is priced: against the naive variant it is worth a computed consumption equivalent in every state carrying productivity-collapse risk.

title: The Atlantic Axis of Football Dominance: An Empirical Investigation of FIFA World Cup Winners

title: Regional Convergence in Tunisia: Evaluating the New District Structure

detail.title: Regional Convergence in Tunisia: Evaluating the New District Structure
detail.abstract: Tunisia's 2023 presidential decree reorganized the country's 24 governorates into five horizontal districts, each deliberately pairing coastal and interior units under shared governance-an institutional response to a coastal-interior divide that has structured the country's economic geography since antiquity. This paper asks whether that regrouping is coherent with Tunisia's actual spatial economy, using a balanced panel of 24 governorates over 2002-2021 and a productivity measure built from confidential firm-level turnover data at the National Institute of Statistics, supplemented with satellite-derived built-up area and nighttime light intensity as infrastructure proxies. A two-way fixed-effects convergence regression finds robust conditional β-convergence in private-sector productivity: interior governorates are catching up to coastal ones, at a 5-year-interval-adjusted speed of roughly 12% a year and a half-life under six years. Spatial error models estimated under both a geographic contiguity matrix and a matrix encoding the district reform's own boundaries detect significant spatial dependence in the residuals-but only at medium-run (5-year) horizons, and only through correlated shocks rather than direct spillovers across governorate lines. Sigma convergence tests within each of the five districts complicate the picture further: only the Greater Tunis district shows significant internal convergence, while two districts straddling the coastal-interior line are significantly diverging internally. The reform's spatial logic is empirically defensible-but coherence with existing geography is not the same as a guarantee of convergence, and the districts most in need of active policy support are precisely the ones showing the least sign of closing internal gaps on their own.

title: The State-Dependent Effects of Fiscal Policy in a Commodity-Exporting Economy
affiliations: Central Reserve Bank of Peru

detail.title: The State-Dependent Effects of Fiscal Policy in a Commodity-Exporting Economy
detail.abstract: This paper asks whether the effectiveness of fiscal policy in a commodity-exporting economy depends on the growth regime of export prices, using Peru as a case study of a small, resource-dependent open economy. I estimate a Bayesian self-exciting threshold VAR (SET-VAR)-applied here for the first time to fiscal policy shocks-in which regimes of high and low export price growth are identified endogenously from the data. In the linear, fixed-coefficient specification, I recover results consistent with the existing literature: government spending shocks are expansionary and tax shocks are contractionary. Conditioning on the export price regime, however, uncovers substantial heterogeneity that the linear estimate masks: fiscal policy is considerably more effective in stimulating output under a high-growth regime, and tax shocks are considerably less contractionary, than under a low-growth regime. These results are consistent with a sovereign risk and financing channel, through which favorable export price shocks relax external borrowing constraints and amplify the transmission of fiscal policy to output-a mechanism supported by the behavior of the EMBIG sovereign spread and by regime-specific differences in the persistence and co-movement of the underlying variables. The findings are robust to a wide battery of alternative specifications and identify export price regimes as a novel dimension of state dependence in fiscal policy, with direct implications for the design of countercyclical fiscal buffers in commodity-exporting economies.

title: Hayek and Economic Development
affiliations: Duke University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Hayek and Economic Development
detail.abstract: Development economics emerged as a field in the 1950s and early 1960s, and in its earliest instantiation it was dubbed "Modernization Theory." If one looks at his published work, it would appear that Friedrich A. Hayek wrote very little about development during this period. This paper suggests that, contrary to the paucity of published evidence, it was a topic in which he was keenly interested. Parts of his published work (e.g., The Road to Serfdom and The Constitution of Liberty) contain thoughts on development issues, but we can see it also in unpublished pieces (e.g., a report on Gibraltar he prepared for the British Colonial Office, lectures he gave at the University of Virginia in 1961), in a radio address that he gave in November 1960, and in his organizing of sessions on development in his role as President of the Mont Pelerin Society in the 1950s that led to a distinctive liberal Mont Pelerin approach to development issues.

title: Computing the Exact Distribution of Predictive Regression ⋆
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management, Nankai University and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Computing the Exact Distribution of Predictive Regression ⋆
detail.abstract: We provide an exact nite sample analysis of a predictive regression whose regressor follows a stationary AR(1) process, giving integral expressions for the densities and distribution functions of the estimated slope coecient, the OLS t-ratio, and the R 2. The obstacle to using such results in practice has been computational: existing methods require the eigenvalues of 2T × 2T matrices, where T is the sample size, an O(T^3) operation, repeated at many quadrature points for the t-ratio and the R 2. We develop algorithms that exploit the near-Toeplitz structure of the problem to evaluate every integrand in O(1) operations, independent of T , so that the cost of an exact distribution no longer grows with the sample size: the distribution of the slope costs milliseconds and those of the t-ratio and the R 2 cost seconds to minutes, at any T. The same algorithms deliver exact moments, including those of the t-ratio, for which no low-dimensional integral representation was previously available. As a by-product of independent interest, we prove a structural property of the matrices involved that identies the correct branch of the complex square root at every point, removing the error-prone tracking of branch-cut crossings that numerical inversion of characteristic functions typically requires.

reference: Working Paper of the Max Planck Institute for Tax Law and Public Finance No. 2026-09
title: Brinkmanship in the Public Eye
affiliations: Max Planck Insitute for Tax Law and Public Finance and

detail.title: Brinkmanship in the Public Eye

publicationDetails.detailsText: Working Paper of the Max Planck Institute for Tax Law and Public Finance No. 2026-09
publicationDetails.journalName: Max Planck Institute for Tax Law & Public Finance Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: What role does the public play in creating uncertainty in economic brinkmanship? Tariffs are once again in public debate, and Trump administration use of tariffs as a coercive tool is particularly evocative of brinkmanship. Uncertain, mutually damaging consequences separate brinkmanship from other bargaining scenarios-but theories are divided on how we should best understand where such uncertainty comes from. To add to this debate, we model bilateral sanctions by separating decision-making across different political actors-namely, executives Leader who propose sanctions and Publics who ratify them through their popular support. Such a design introduces the necessary uncertainty for brinkmanship through private information on citizen preferences: neither Leader is sure of what the Publics want, and thus threats of tariffs become uncertain and potentially mutual damaging. Through this design, we thus advance a novel understanding of where uncertainty can come from in interstate bargains.

title: The Bet
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Bet
detail.abstract: Chekhov's lawyer sells fifteen years of his life for two million roubles and then, five hours before the term expires, walks out and forfeits. We give a mathematical model of the contract. The bet is strictly negative-sum in money-the fifteen years are burned rather than transferredso it cannot exist between agents who value only money, whatever their priors. We then show that no pair (D, u) of discount function and utility fixed over the fifteen years rationalises the story: the escalation from the banker's proposed five years to fifteen is strictly dominated at an unchanged prize, and so is the exit. A signalling explanation is also excluded, because the observed term exceeds the least-cost separating term by a factor of nearly four given the banker's stated beliefs. What remains is that the term is an input rather than an output-a dosage. Modelling the lawyer's utility of money as a Brownian motion with drift, the escalation from five years to fifteen raises the probability of the sign change from 0.25 to 0.90 at the calibration matching the story. We then prove that the renunciation problem has no maximiser: its payoff rises on [0, T) and drops at T , so the supremum is approached but never attained; five hours is 3.80 × 10-5 of the term, a deliberate ε bought to secure a discontinuity. A settlement window stands open for the first eight and a half years and closes at the transformation time without either party being able to observe it. The banker meanwhile holds a short position in the reciprocal of his own wealth, with E[M/W T ] = (M/W 0)e (σ 2-µ)T diverging whenever drift falls short of variance, and the contemplated murder is the exercise of an embedded default option. Finally, a wager whose stake is correlated with the bettor's solvency does not deliver a valid e-value: long-dated bets are structurally poor instruments of evidence.

title: Bilateral Trade Between China and the EU: Growth, Integration, and Policy Uncertainty
affiliations: University of Barcelona - Regional Quantitative Analysis Group (AQR-IREA) and Ramon Llull University - IQS School of Management

detail.title: Bilateral Trade Between China and the EU: Growth, Integration, and Policy Uncertainty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors state that there is no conflict of interests. The funders had no role in the design of the study; in the collection, analyses, or interpretation of data; in the writing of the manuscript, or in the decision to publish the results.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Spanish Ministry of Science and Innovation (MCIN) / Agencia Estatal de Investigación under the project PID2023-146073NB-I00.

detail.abstract: This paper examines trade flows between China and the European Union from 2000 to 2022, emphasizing the role of trade policy uncertainty as a key determinant of bilateral trade. Using an extended gravity model, we introduce a novel measure of China's Trade Policy Uncertainty (TPU) and show that it has a significant and persistent negative relationship with China-EU trade, even after accounting for traditional economic and institutional factors. While China's economic growth constitutes a dominant driver of trade, the results underline the anticipatory nature of flows in response to rising uncertainty. Furthermore, our findings indicate, although evidence of trade gains associated with formal participation in the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) remains limited at the aggregate level, positive effects are identified for EU exports to China. Robustness checks across alternative specifications highlight the usefulness of TPU indicators as early warning tools for shifts in trade dynamics. These insights can help policymakers better anticipate disruptions and design resilient strategies for stability and economic integration.

title: Forecasting Global Inflation: The Rise of Machine Learning
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Forecasting Global Inflation: The Rise of Machine Learning
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether integrating a high-dimensional cross section of global macroeconomic and financial indicators through regularized machine learning algorithms produces superior out-of-sample forecasts of global inflation compared to standard econometric baselines. We construct a GDP-weighted global inflation aggregate to serve as the target variable and compile a high-dimensional dataset of 103 macroeconomic predictors spanning February 1999 to July 2026. The empirical evaluation relies on a recursive pseudo-out-of-sample design covering 30,256 hyperparameter permutations across four forecast horizons. The specification grid evaluates traditional autoregressive and random walk models against machine learning estimators, including regularized linear regressions, kernel methods, tree-based ensembles, and deep neural networks, utilizing principal component extraction to handle multicollinearity. The results indicate that regularized machine learning algorithms and dynamic forecast combinations generated via inverse mean squared error weighting yield lower root mean squared errors than univariate benchmarks. Support vector regressions with a linear kernel and Gaussian process models dominate at the short and long horizons, respectively, while gated recurrent units minimize errors at the six-month interval. The predictive advantage of the high-dimensional framework becomes evident during the structural variance expansion following the 2020 global economic shock, where traditional autoregressive forecasts suffer performance degradation. Forecast encompassing tests confirm that the machine learning models provide significant complementary informational content not captured by standard baselines. Finally, an analysis of variable importance reveals that the predictive accuracy is primarily driven by business inventories, corporate bond spreads, and broad money supply aggregates.

title: The Faustian Bargain
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Faustian Bargain
detail.abstract: Faust sells an infinite good for a finite one: twenty-four years. We show that this trade is governed entirely by the quantiles of the discount measure µ D (dt) ∝ D(t) dt. The fair term is its median, a tithe is its first decile, and the Faustian ratio is its odds, so the log price of a soul is a logit. Three structural results follow. Propriety: eternity has a finite price if and only if ∞ 0 D < ∞, which for completely monotone D with Bernstein mixing measure ν says E ν [1/r] < ∞; otherwise the correct comparison is an overtaking criterion. Mortality restores propriety for every mortal, and at zero pure time preference the price of a soul is the median stationary residual lifetime, so it is immortality rather than patience that makes the bargain incoherent. Rigidity: the Faustmann land expectation value has the Faustian odds as its denominator and admits its closed form only under exponential discounting, becoming a Hurwitz zeta function under gamma discounting; within the completely monotone class it is biased rather than merely special, understating bare land value at every rotation length by a Jensen gap of a factor 2.3 at a standard calibration. Two impatiences: hyperbolic tails raise the price of eternity without bound while present bias destroys it below a critical value. A bilateral theorem identifies the counterparty: a soul trades at term T only if the buyer's discount measure places less mass on [0, T ] than the seller's, and a buyer whose measure is improper will sign any contract at any price.

title: Corporate Fake News: Determinants, Market Consequences, and Corporate Responses
affiliations: , The Chinese University of Hong Kong and University of Technology Sydney (UTS)

detail.title: Corporate Fake News: Determinants, Market Consequences, and Corporate Responses
detail.abstract: Using a comprehensive dataset of 12,736 fake news articles published during 2016–2020, we examine the determinants and market consequences of corporate fake news. We find that 13 percent of S&P 1500 firms are targeted by fake news. These firms have greater readership appeal, operate in uncertain and belief-sensitive information environments, and score low on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings. Following negative fake news, firms experience a statistically significant drop of 0.094 percent in abnormal returns, which is approximately a sixth of the market reaction to matched credible news, and this price impact dissipates by day two. The market reaction is driven by noise traders and firms with high arbitrage impediments, consistent with our hypothesis that boundedly rational investors lead to correlated value-irrelevant trading that sophisticated investors cannot fully arbitrage away due to transaction costs. Lastly, we find that 21 percent of target firms disclose fake news risks or directly respond to fake news during conference calls, underscoring the economic significance of fake news to public firms.

title: Bayesian Stratified Sampling and Portfolio Selection: A Finite-Population View
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Bayesian Stratified Sampling and Portfolio Selection: A Finite-Population View
detail.abstract: Implementing a decile portfolio means holding a subset of it, and the subsets are large: a decile of a broad universe runs to a thousand names. We treat this as finite-population sampling. The benchmark is a population total, the portfolio an estimator of it, and the error a prediction error on the unheld complement in the sense of Royall [1970]. For an arbitrary covariance matrix, the anticipated squared error of an n-name sample from an N-name stratum is D(1/n-1/N), where D = σ2-c is the average variance less the average covariance. Since portfolio variance is c + D/n, the constituent variance splits as σ2 = c + D into a part that floors the risk problem and a part that governs the replication problem, and the two are disjoint. Tracking error therefore falls as within-decile correlation rises: writing Σ = σ 2 e I + σ 2 a 11 ′ , a contrast (1 ′ d = 0) annihilates the common component that the budget constraint (1 ′ w = 1) maximises. Markowitz did not write on replication by sampling, but his 1952 objection to the law of large numbers states the contrary intuition exactly, and it is correct for his objective and inverted for this one. The Bayesian development identifies a stratum with an exchangeability class in the sense of Kingman [1978], which forces the rank-one covariance rather than assuming it; Polson and Sokolov [2026] then prove the 1/N rule exactly optimal under all exchangeable beliefs by averaging over the N ! permutationsvariance is constant on each orbit, the orbit average of every feasible portfolio is equal weight, and convexity does the rest, the cost of any deviation d being σ 2 e ∥d∥ 2 , the same meter that prices tracking error. The development also makes the predictive distribution of tracking error Student-t on n-1 degrees of freedom, and isolates ignorability-which fails whenever names are chosen on unmodelled views, inflating deviation sixfold in simulation. The same decomposition applied to the Kelly criterion splits growth into a directional term that correlation caps and a cross-sectional term proportional to 1/D that correlation subsidises; since D now sits in a denominator, Kelly leverage is fragile to the correlation estimate exactly where replication is robust to it. Implementation requires one number per stratum, estimable from the cross-section alone. In a calibrated illustration, four hundred names reproduce a ten-decile strategy spanning 3,490 securities to 1.52% tracking error at 6.2% of the cost of full replication.

title: Do Bank Mergers Improve Asset Quality? Evidence from India's Public Sector Bank Consolidation
affiliations: Ton Duc Thang University

detail.title: Do Bank Mergers Improve Asset Quality? Evidence from India's Public Sector Bank Consolidation
detail.abstract: Whether large-scale bank consolidation can improve asset quality remains an important yet unresolved question, particularly in emerging banking systems where non-performing assets pose persistent challenges to financial stability. This study examines the asset-quality effects of India's 2020 public sector bank consolidation, one of the country's most significant stateled banking restructuring initiatives. Using panel data from 24 listed commercial banks over 2016-2024, we exploit the reform as a quasi-natural experiment and employ a difference-indifferences framework to compare changes in asset quality between affected and unaffected banks. The results show that banks exposed to the consolidation experienced a significant improvement in asset quality relative to their unaffected counterparts following the reform. These findings provide evidence that bank consolidation can facilitate balance-sheet repair by reducing asset-quality deterioration in a banking system characterized by persistent nonperforming assets.

title: Bayesian Fermi Problems
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Bayesian Fermi Problems
detail.abstract: A Fermi problem asks for the order of magnitude of a quantity that cannot be looked up: the number of piano tuners in Chicago, the mass of a cumulus cloud, the number of communicating civilisations in the galaxy. The standard recipe-decompose the target into a product of factors, bracket each factor between plausible bounds, take the geometric mean-is presented in the popular literature as a heuristic. It is in fact an exact Bayesian procedure. Bracketing is prior elicitation on the log scale; the geometric mean of a bracket is both the posterior median and the Bayes rule under log-quadratic loss, for any dependence structure; and the scale invariance of the problem singles out the Jeffreys prior π(Q) ∝ 1/Q, which yields Benford's law for leading digits. We then give the error propagation theory that explains why the recipe works, together with a distribution-free bound on the usable length of a chain of reasoning, and we quantify the two failure modes: systematic log-bias, which grows linearly in n, and correlated factors, which degrade the √ n rate to n √ ρ. An effective chain length measures the cancellation a decomposition actually achieves, and a variance criterion says when refining a factor is worth doing. The variance share of a factor equals 1e-2I for I its mutual information with the target, turning "where should I spend the next hour?" into an exact information calculation. We also treat logarithmic pooling with global-local shrinkage, in which correlated opinions are discounted through an effective crowd size; updating on hard constraints; the number of digits an estimate earns; and calibration, where an estimator's overconfidence is a single parameter estimable from quiz answers and shown to inflate the chain length he believes he can attempt. Six worked examples run from piano tuners and cloud mass through Taylor's blast-wave recovery of the Trinity yield and the electricity demand of AI data centres to the Drake equation and a scale-invariant analysis unifying Gott's ∆t argument with the German tank problem.

title: Generative Bayesian Computation for Particle Filtering and Learning
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and George Mason University

detail.title: Generative Bayesian Computation for Particle Filtering and Learning
detail.abstract: Generative Bayesian Computation (GBC) methods are developed for particle filtering and learning. Our central result writes the filtering step as a recursion for the quantile function of the filter: the Bayes update is an inverse distortion of the uniform base measure and propagation is a composition of monotone maps. By the quantile theory of Parzen, quantile functions compose and hence act as deep learners; the filtering quantile function is a deep network whose layers are indexed by time and whose weights are determined by the data. Sequential Bayesian computation thus becomes supervised learning: an implicit quantile neural network trained on simulated paths provides an amortized posterior, delivering filtering draws for any dataset by evaluation. Particle learning emerges as the Monte Carlo quadrature of the recursion, resampling as inversion of the distortion and propagation as composition, with conditional sufficient statistics supplying Rao-Blackwellized training data. For mixture models the allocation update is a discrete distortion and the predictive quantile function is a gated network. Filtered functionals admit an O(N-4) quantile integration bound, and examples spanning Gaussian learning, the local level model, stochastic volatility and mixtures reproduce exact posterior quantiles. Finally, we conclude with directions for future research.

title: The Mathematics of Lightning
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Mathematics of Lightning
detail.abstract: A lightning flash is a free-boundary problem for Laplace's equation driven by a stochastic breakdown rule. This note assembles its mathematics under three headings. On shape: the electrostatic energy is a monotone decreasing functional of the ionised set, so growth runs downhill, and the resulting moving-boundary problem ∇ 2 ϕ = 0, v n = µ|∇ϕ| η is unstable at every wavenumber, with σ k = V |k|. The instability is scale-free, so the channel tip-splits at all scales above a regularisation length that sets the branch spacing, and the limiting set is a random fractal. The discrete law is the dielectric breakdown model, whose growth measure is the η-th power of harmonic measure: η = 1 is the diffusion rule, η = 2 the local dissipation rule. The exponent is not free but the logarithmic sensitivity of the propagation law, η = B/(E/p) from the Townsend coefficient, giving η ≈ 1.8 at a streamer head and depending on the reduced field alone. Simulation gives D = 1.73 ± 0.01 at η = 1, and the growth measure is multifractal with τ ′ (1) = 1.04 against Makarov's exact 1 and αmin = 0.56 against Beurling's bound 1 2. A third mechanism is quenched disorder: the channel minimises a random action, a directed polymer with KPZ wandering exponent ζ = 2/3. On inference: the growth law is exactly a conditional logit in η with covariate log |∇ϕ|, so the log-likelihood is concave and the Fisher information is a within-choice-set variance; the score is a martingale in the growth filtration, so observed information gives valid standard errors despite complete dependence; in simulation η is recovered to within two standard errors from a single cluster, with per-step information falling from 1.97 to 0.33 as η rises from 0.5 to 2, because greedy growth is uninformative about how greedy it is. Freezing of the multifractal spectrum, collapse of the dimension to one and loss of identifiability are the same limit. On energy: nothing disappears. Poynting's theorem localises every transfer as ∂ t u em + ∇ • S =-J • E, and a flash of some 3 × 10 9 J becomes dissociation and ionisation enthalpy, a cylindrical Sedov-Taylor blast wave, thunder, light, nitric oxide and finally ambient heat, generating ∆S ≈ 10 7 J K-1 ; the geometry enters the ledger through the total channel length L ≈ ℓ c (H/ℓ c) D. The familiar "missing" ninety-nine per cent is an observational deficit, not a violation of conservation.

title: Elo Ratings, Implied Volatility and Kelly Betting in Sports Prediction Markets
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Elo Ratings, Implied Volatility and Kelly Betting in Sports Prediction Markets
detail.abstract: Sports event contracts on regulated exchanges such as Kalshi trade at prices that are direct probability statements. This paper develops a statistical framework for pricing and trading such contracts. Three ingredients are combined. First, the sports model of Aldous (2017), in which the probability that A beats B is a function of a strength difference, together with the Elo rating algorithm viewed as stochastic approximation. Second, the hierarchical aging and era-bridging models of Berry et al. (1999), which supply structured priors on how strengths evolve with age and across eras. Third, the Brownian motion model of Stern (1994) and its implied volatility formulation in Polson and Stern (2015), which converts point spreads and moneylines into a win probability martingale and makes ingame trading a form of volatility trading. Position sizing follows the Kelly criterion in the tradition of Kelly (1956) and Thorp (2006). A key identity is that the optimal growth rate from betting a model probability q against a market price π equals the Kullback-Leibler divergence KL(q ∥ π) between belief and price, so that edge is information. We derive the total quadratic variation of the win probability process, connect the favorite-longshot bias to calibration of Elo forecasts, and give simulation evidence on rating dynamics, fractional Kelly and in-game price volatility. Limitations, including estimation risk, fees and adverse selection, are treated explicitly.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Autonomous Systems and the Future of Legal Responsibility

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Autonomous Systems and the Future of Legal Responsibility
detail.abstract: Fault-based and even strict-liability doctrines share an assumption that is quietly failing in the age of autonomous systems: that harm can be traced to a discrete, identifiable decision. Reinforcement-learned and continuously updated systems now generate outcomes that no designer selected, no operator approved, and no single dataset predicted. This article examines the resulting "emergent-behavior gap"-the doctrinal space in which an autonomous system's harmful output is neither a manufacturing defect, a negligent act, nor a foreseeable design consequence, but the product of adaptive processes that exceed the causal categories liability law was built to trace. Using comparative doctrinal analysis across the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, South Korea, and Brazil, and engaging jurisprudence including OQ v Land Hessen (C-634/21), Mobley v. Workday, and Uber B.V. v. Aslam, the article argues that existing regimes-the EU's revised Product Liability Directive, U.S. state tort law, the UK Automated Vehicles Act 2024, and comparable Asian and South American frameworks-remain adequate for foreseeable-risk harms but structurally incapable of allocating responsibility for genuinely emergent ones. It proposes the Emergent Autonomy Liability Standard (EALS): a tiered architecture combining certification-anchored strict liability for classified risk profiles, mandatory behavioral logging ("autonomy black boxes") to preserve causal traceability, and a no-fault compensation fund, financed by risk-tiered contributions, for harms that resist reconstruction under either fault or strict-liability analysis. The article's original contribution is to reframe the AI-liability debate away from who controlled the system toward whether the harm is causally reconstructible at all, and to show why that distinction, not the degree of automation itself, should determine which liability instrument applies.

title: The Velocity of Capital

detail.title: The Velocity of Capital
detail.abstract: This paper quantifies the aggregate annual economic benefit of the U.S. dollar's global reserve currency status, estimating a central range of $1.4 to $1.9 trillion-equivalent to roughly 5-6.5% of U.S. GDP-a figure that appears in no national account and is largely absent from public and policy debate. The analysis decomposes the privilege into five structurally distinct, sourced channels: (1) a system-wide borrowing cost advantage across the $50 trillion U.S. fixed income market; (2) a suppressed equity discount rate that sustains $10-12 trillion of incremental public and private equity market capitalization; (3) a capital-formation multiplier effect operating through venture capital and private equity deal flow; (4) a trade-structure dividend arising from the Triffin dynamic, combining consumer price savings with the services-sector reallocation gain, presented alongside an explicit accounting of its concentrated distributional costs to manufacturing communities; and (5) residual pillars including seigniorage, dollar-clearing financial infrastructure, and sanctions capacity. An explicit overlap adjustment is applied between the capital-formation and trade-structure channels to avoid double-counting. The paper also models a term-premium normalization scenario-independent of, and larger than, the reserve-currency effect itself-under which continued Treasury issuance could compress justified equity multiples by a further 17-22%. The paper concludes that the dollar's privilege is a structural advantage requiring active stewardship rather than a permanent endowment, and that its magnitude should inform debates on fiscal sustainability, trade policy, and the use of sanctions.

title: Human-Capital Beta, Career Options, and the Compensation of Former Regulators
affiliations: University of Leicester

detail.title: Human-Capital Beta, Career Options, and the Compensation of Former Regulators

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest exists
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper develops a structural career-option model of regulator human-capital beta, defined as the firm-level exposure of value and compensation to regulatory expertise. The framework is motivated by evidence that financial firms hiring former regulators experience positive announcement returns, pay compensation premia, and obtain performance effects that are specific to regulatory rather than generic government experience. Regulatory expertise, rule interpretation, and policy-signal quality enter as primitives that shift project cash flows, regulatory costs, financing conditions, and market beliefs. Human-capital beta summarizes the firm-level exposure to those primitives. A regulator's private-sector opportunity is represented as a convex career claim on firm equity value, with the public-sector continuation value serving as the strike-like outside option. The model generates three main implications. First, announcement returns are increasing in regulatory exposure and agency-firm match quality. Second, compensation premia arise because the same expertise that raises firm value also raises the value of the regulator's career option. Third, when equity-linked compensation, leverage, and weak debt penalties interact, value-enhancing regulatory human capital can also move a firm toward a leverage-vega default-risk boundary. The paper does not assume that all revolving-door moves are opportunistic; instead, it identifies the subset of career paths in which regulatory human capital is capitalized into firm value and private compensation is equity-linked.

title: Frontier Settlement and Nation Building: Evidence from Tuntian in Historical China
affiliations: Jinan University,  and Wuhan University

detail.title: Frontier Settlement and Nation Building: Evidence from Tuntian in Historical China
detail.abstract: How did China-a vast and historically diverse empire-develop such a culturally unified identity over the long run? This paper examines the enduring role of tuntian, a state-led system of frontier settlement implemented across dynasties from 400 to 1900 CE. Using a novel prefecture level dataset, we show that while tuntian served immediate administrative and military aims, it also set in motion a lasting process of cultural and ethnic integration. Regions with longer exposure to tuntian exhibit sustained declines in cultural diversity measured by surname and ethnic composition, and stronger alignment with a common national identity. Residents in these regions also exhibit higher levels of social trust, particularly toward weak ties, indicating a deeper sense of social cohesion across groups. These effects are driven by two complementary channels, namely the diffusion of culture through state-induced migration, which reduced linguistic barriers across regions, and the intergenerational transmission of identity preferences. Overall, this study reveals how a historical institution not originally designed for cultural assimilation could, through sustained demographic exposure and social interaction, shape the formation of national identity over centuries.

detail.abstract: The near disappearance of traditional defined benefit pensions is often treated as a loss for retirement security. This paper asks a different question: whether workers and employers value guaranteed pension benefits enough to bear their full economic cost. ERISA made private pensions more secure but also more expensive, after which traditional plans declined sharply. Meanwhile, workers with defined contribution accounts generally do not recreate DB features through higher saving, conservative portfolios, or annuitization. These patterns do not prove that DB pensions lack value, but they suggest limited willingness to pay the marginal cost of sustaining guarantees under economics-based funding standards.

title: The Economics of Climate Stabilization: Investment, Technology Diffusion, and the Transition from Emissions Growth to Global Net-Zero

detail.title: The Economics of Climate Stabilization: Investment, Technology Diffusion, and the Transition from Emissions Growth to Global Net-Zero
detail.abstract:
The report argues that achieving global net‑zero emissions is not primarily a cost burden but a macroeconomic opportunity driven by rapid, endogenous technological learning. As stated in the Executive Summary, “the cumulative macroeconomic benefits of rapid technology diffusion will outpace transition costs by a factor of 3 to 1 globally” and that accelerating learning rates in solar, storage, and green industrial systems are pushing zero‑carbon energy below fossil baseload costs.

Climate stabilization is framed as a thermodynamic constraint—CO₂ accumulation must cease—requiring absolute decoupling of GDP from emissions. The report highlights that electrified systems offer structural efficiency advantages and that decarbonization propagates through industrial and urban nodes, reducing downstream supply‑chain emissions.

A central thesis is that technology diffusion follows S‑curve dynamics, with Wright’s Law driving cost‑curve compressions across solar PV, batteries, wind, hydrogen, heat pumps, and advanced nuclear. As fossil asset terminal values decline, capital reallocates toward clean infrastructure, accelerating adoption.

The report identifies a $3–$4 trillion annual investment gap and emphasizes blended finance, sovereign guarantees, and standardized green taxonomies as essential mechanisms. Clean‑energy investment is positioned as a global economic stimulus with higher multipliers than fossil investments.

Finally, the report stresses multi‑system resilience—supergrids, storage, demand‑response, and AI‑driven grid orchestration—and the necessity of robust carbon pricing, regulatory mandates, and CBAMs. Regional analyses show that emerging economies will determine global outcomes, with technology leapfrogging offering pathways for industrialization and poverty reduction.

The conclusion frames climate mitigation as the foundation of the next macroeconomic supercycle, where leaders in clean‑technology deployment capture disproportionate economic gains.

detail.abstract: This chapter argues that municipal debt monitoring is an important but underappreciated component of retirement security. Municipalities promise pensions and retiree health benefits, debt repayment, public services, and tax stability from the same fiscal capacity, so fiscal deterioration forces tradeoffs among these claimants. Effective monitoring requires acquiring, verifying, using, and acting on fiscal information before imbalances become acute. We argue that monitoring failures in this market are structural rather than incidental, reflecting fragmented principals, weak incentives, opaque disclosure, and limited enforcement. Professional intermediaries lower information costs but hold narrow mandates, leaving no actor with both the incentive and authority to safeguard fiscal sustainability.

title: Greece: Navigating in Turbulent Waters
affiliations: Bard College - Levy Economics Institute,  and University of Cassino - Department of Economics

detail.title: Greece: Navigating in Turbulent Waters
detail.abstract: The news on the condition of the Greek economy presents a continuing success story compared with the average EU member states, unless a more careful examination is undertaken. Announcements of positive aspects of the economy are overemphasized while the troubling trends are either not widely reported or are reported as insignificant. Government-friendly research organizations—think tanks and the research departments of major systemic banks—including government agencies, praise the efficient and effective management of the economy. To be sure, statistical releases from the Bank of Greece and the Hellenic Statistical Agency (Elstat) report some positive trends: growth of output, declining “official” unemployment rates, increases in the minimum monthly wage, PMI, public and private investment, and fiscal discipline—accomplished through a combination of larger tax revenue collection and primary expenditure limitations—delivering primary surpluses. The latter increases the country’s credibility in financial markets, reflected in higher credit ratings for Greek government bonds and relatively lower interest rates than in past periods that reduce the cost of borrowing.

detail.abstract: Can operator-theoretic persistence and tail-risk diagnostics provide advance warning of leveraged portfolio fragility? We examine this question using the July 2026 collapse of Situational Awareness-an AI-focused fund-as a natural experiment in concentration, shifting dependence, leverage, and forced liquidation. Combining a reconstruction of the fund's June 30 Form 13F long book with the Clock-of-Regimes (COR) framework, we map regime occupancy, tail exposure, and operator persistence into a first-passage survival model. The disclosed portfolio was highly concentrated: SanDisk and Micron comprised 55.6% of reported 13F value, the top six positions held 81.0%, and a nine-name core (88.3% of value) exhibited realized July pairwise correlations between 0.75 and 0.92. At the key prospective observation date (July 21), despite a composite Yellow zone, COR indicated full stress occupancy (𝑃 3 = 1.000), stress volatility 𝜎 3 = 3.54% per day, tail exposure q = 0.0486, entrapment radius 𝜌(𝑁) = 95.2, and aggregate residence tr(𝑁) = 162.8. Compared to an unconditional state-mixture benchmark holding portfolio mechanics and Student-𝑡 emissions fixed, COR conditioning increases estimated eight-session first-passage failure probabilities from 0.22% to 1.77% at 2× leverage; 4.25% to 13.00% at 2.5×; 16.09% to 30.64% at 3×; and 50.60% to 63.95% at 4×. COR does not forecast return direction; rather, it identifies when market persistence and financing constraints render previously admissible leverage untenable.

title: Balancing Financial Inclusion with Integrity: A Path Forward for Nepal

detail.title: Balancing Financial Inclusion with Integrity: A Path Forward for Nepal

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Banking, Finance and Insurance, Volume 7, Pp.1-13. Banking, Finance and Insurance Institute of Nepal (BFIN), Annual Journal, 2026.

detail.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to shed light on how a country like Nepal, which is under FATF's increased monitoring list, can balance the financial inclusion and financial integrity goals. When a country is added to the grey list, financial institutions and supervisors are likely to heighten their vigilance, which may hinder financial inclusion. This paper outlines the recommended actions to ensure that financial inclusion is not compromised while addressing AML/CFT deficiencies. This paper explores how some other countries are using flexibility in FATF standards by applying simplified measures for low-risk customers. The paper then analyzes the current customer due diligence framework of Nepal, identifies the shortcomings with respect to the use of simplified CDD measures and outlines specific reform measures Nepal should take to bolster financial inclusion without compromising financial integrity. The main findings of the paper is that there is significant gap in Nepal's CDD framework with respect to flexibility on applying simplified measures. Nepal has not adequately identified low-risk customers, lacks clarity in regulation regarding document requirements in simplified CDD, and doesn't have sufficient guidance on applying simplified measures. This is an original work that identifies shortcomings in Nepal's CDD framework, which could hinder financial inclusion. The author believes that the recommended reform measures can support Nepal's financial inclusion efforts. These findings and recommendations may also be valuable for other countries that have elevated ML/TF risks and are making efforts to enhance financial inclusion.

title: Economic Prospects for the United States: Is the Current K-shaped Economy Sustainable?
affiliations: Bard College - Levy Economics Institute,  and University of Cassino - Department of Economics

detail.title: Economic Prospects for the United States: Is the Current K-shaped Economy Sustainable?
detail.abstract: The latest report from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) indicates that nominal consumer spending increased in May 2026 by 0.7% from the previous month, but in real terms the increase was recorded at 0.3%. As we will discuss later, the decomposition of consumers into various household categories will show a mixed picture that doesn’t appear encouraging toward equality.

title: Knwoledge and Venture Funding: Complementarities and Financial Contracts

detail.title: Knwoledge and Venture Funding: Complementarities and Financial Contracts
detail.abstract: In this paper I analyse venture capital finance using the tools provided by the literature on the economics of innovation, in particular the notion of localised technological knowledge and the resource-based theory of the firm, to build a model of financial contracting. This entails that, instead of looking exclusively at financial indicators or monetary incentives, I will deepen the knowledge connection between the venture capitalist and the financed firm, as the benchmark to understand the potential of this source of finance. Consistent with evidence regarding venture funding, the model portrays a separation between a financial and a nonfinancial part of the venture investment, which is reflected in a “dichotomy” among the investors. In fact, the model shows that the success of a venture program is strictly linked to the knowledge flow inspired and reinforced by the complementarities between the knowledge bases of entrepreneur and venture capitalist, instead to a particular financing scheme as sustained by most of the literature. The model can also suggest a new methodology to analyse other intermediaries, always exploiting the central role of knowledge in designing financial contracts.

title: Human-on-the-Loop: A Theory of Oversight Capacity, Its Failure Modes, and the Non-Delegable Residual in the Age of AI Agents

detail.title: Human-on-the-Loop: A Theory of Oversight Capacity, Its Failure Modes, and the Non-Delegable Residual in the Age of AI Agents
detail.abstract: Firms deploying AI agents increasingly describe their governance posture as human-onthe-loop: the system executes autonomously while a human defines purpose, values and capital allocation, exercises governance, and intervenes at exceptions. This paper takes that proposition seriously enough to test it, and finds that it cannot be adopted as written. Three reclassifications follow. First, loop position is not a stance management adopts but an authority configuration whose feasibility is fixed by the ratio of a decision class's consequence latency to the overseer's measured end-to-end response latency; throughput, not policy, determines where a firm sits. Second, oversight is not a role but a consumable resource with a measurable capacity-uncommitted attention, interaction time, context re-acquisition cost, neglect time-and therefore with a solvency condition. Insolvent oversight fails not by refusing work but by accepting it, and its symptom is a rising override and non-response rate. Third, the human's irreplaceable contribution is not superior judgement but verification independence: a loop closed by a verifier statistically dependent on its generator does not converge on correctness, a claim that survives improvements in model capability only where an instrument maintains the overseer's detection probability as prevalence falls. The five roles then separate by scaling law. Constitutive oversight-purpose, admissible means, and the allocation of capital and attention across purposes-costs O(1) in agent throughput; control oversight admits no corresponding bound at a fixed detection guarantee, since under a fixed attention budget the share of consequential errors it removes falls as O(1/T), and strictly faster wherever the supervised system's reliability is improving, while holding that share at any positive constant costs attention growing as Ω(T) and strictly faster still. Routing exceptions selectively relocates that constraint to the recall of the routing rule rather than removing it. Any configuration financed by rising throughput therefore reaches a point beyond which only constitutive oversight remains solvent, which is what makes a reconstructed model implementable. The paper is a conceptual contribution carrying a formal capacity constraint and a measurement proposal; it generates no new data. It builds from the refutation set-human factors, human-computer interaction, agent evaluation, public administration and primary legal records-and closes with a protocol requiring a firm that asserts human oversight to state the quantities that would make the assertion true or false.

title: Trading Through the Shock: Physical Climate Events and Transaction Continuity in China's Corporate Bond Market

detail.title: Trading Through the Shock: Physical Climate Events and Transaction Continuity in China's Corporate Bond Market
detail.abstract: Physical climate risk can raise expected credit losses without necessarily causing an immediate breakdown in market functioning. This paper studies whether localized extreme-heat and extreme-rain episodes disrupt short-run transaction continuity in China's exchange-traded corporate bond market. I link public daily histories for 513 bonds issued by 93 exactly matched listed legal entities to 1,011 issuer-specific weather events across 33 registered-office locations. Conventional and small-cluster wild-bootstrap tests do not detect a common deterioration in zero trading, traded-bond share, or reported volume. One-sided five-day harm limits are +2.1 percentage points,-1.7 percentage points, and-20.8%, respectively. Because the candidate margins were chosen after descriptive inspection, I interpret them through a full sensitivity grid: the data exclude only moderate increases of 3-5 percentage points in zero trading, declines of 2-5 percentage points in traded-bond share, and volume declines of 25-30%, not tighter changes. Strict balanced-window diagnostics using the strongest annual event, every eligible episode, and conservative 20-and 60-market-day terminal no-trade extensions do not reveal a common breakdown. Rain-tail placebo estimates reverse sign across 20-, 40-, and 60-market-day shifts, and none survives Holm correction. Public histories cannot distinguish maturity, delisting, suspension, default, or data loss after the last quote, and the final sample is tilted toward larger, higher-rated issuers. The evidence therefore supports transaction continuity in a selected segment, not complete price discovery or immunity from latent credit loss.

title: Political Polarization, Vote-share Competition, and Endogenous Abstention
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata - Faculty of Economics and Universitas Mercatorum

detail.title: Political Polarization, Vote-share Competition, and Endogenous Abstention

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest
declarations.funderStatement: The paper received no funding

detail.abstract: We study political competition when voters may abstain because neither candidate is ideologically close enough to justify participation in a framework of increasing polarization. We study the effect of polarization by introducing a symmetric family of voter distributions that moves continuously from center-peaked to uniform to U-shaped while leaving the median voter fixed. Candidates maximize their share of votes cast, the electoral analogue of marketshare competition in the Hotelling model. With stable left-right party identities, the unique equilibrium is convergence at the median when the electorate is center-peaked and maximal feasible divergence when it is U-shaped; the uniform distribution is the knife-edge between the two regimes. Candidate divergence has an important compositional effect on participation. It initially remobilizes previously alienated extremists but, once candidate constituencies cease to overlap, creates abstention among moderates. For sufficiently strong divergence, the electorate that actually votes becomes more polarized than the underlying eligible electorate. We derive a unique threshold at which this polarization reversal occurs and obtain its comparative statics. Greater underlying voter polarization raises the required degree of candidate divergence, while a larger ideological reservation distance lowers it. In the U-shaped equilibrium, when candidate divergence leaves a politically unrepresented center, equilibrium divergence necessarily exceeds this threshold: all residual abstention is centrist and the voting electorate is more polarized than the population from which it is drawn. A dynamic extension shows how gradual candidate adjustment can generate rising abstention followed by turnout recovery even while moderate citizens progressively disappear from electoral participation.

title:
A Study on Street Food Entrepreneurship in the UAE: 
Untapped Potential and Global Opportunities

detail.title:
A Study on Street Food Entrepreneurship in the UAE: 
Untapped Potential and Global Opportunities
detail.abstract: Street food business is a major driver of employment, cultural diversity, and domestic GDP in most developing economies, as it has been the case with India. In the UAE, renowned for its cosmopolitan food culture, high-end dining, and increasing demand for diversity, the prospects of a dynamic street food economy are yet to be fully explored. As tourism and cultural openness grows, there is potential for the UAE to utilize its multicultural populace to provide a managed street food economy for the benefit of both locals and expatriates. The current market condition, problems, opportunities, and its positioning with international food trends are examined in this research regarding street food entrepreneurship in the UAE. The venture will determine whether street food, traditionally considered an informal sector, can be a formal and innovative component of the UAE's food and hospitality industry.

title: Tokenizing Mickey Mantle and Charizard: Vaulted Digital Twins and the Financialization of Sports and Trading Cards
affiliations: Marquette University

detail.title: Tokenizing Mickey Mantle and Charizard: Vaulted Digital Twins and the Financialization of Sports and Trading Cards
detail.abstract: This paper examines the emerging use of blockchain-based tokens to facilitate the custody, transfer, and potential fractionalization of sports and trading cards. It presents a comparative case-study analysis of platforms that connect digital tokens to vaulted physical cards, with particular attention to authentication, redemption, custody, transaction costs, and legal classification. The analysis distinguishes one-to-one tokenization, where a token is associated with a particular physical card, from fractionalization, which divides economic interests in an underlying asset among multiple holders. The paper uses Vorsatz's 2019 theoretical model of collectibles tokenization to identify a potential tradeoff between liquidity-related gains and the consumption value associated with physical access and display. It also considers Kanellopoulos and his colleagues' evidence that digital NBA Top Shot platform affected selected physical card outcomes on eBay as a related but distinct example of competition between native digital and physical collectibles. The case studies suggest that vault-backed tokenization may reduce certain transfer, shipping, and custody frictions while creating reliance on platform terms, custody arrangements, redemption procedures, and the legal relationship between the token holder and the underlying card. Fractionalization raises additional questions concerning investor rights, disclosure, tax treatment, and potential securities-law characterization. The paper concludes that the economic welfare, market-displacement, and regulatory consequences of tokenized physical cards remain empirical questions requiring platform-level transaction data, contractual analysis, and consumer-demand evidence.

affiliations: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Center for Transportation & Logistics

detail.title: Delivering Resilient Housing Solutions After Disasters: Roundtable Report, MIT Humanitarian Supply Chain Lab

publicationDetails.detailsText: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper No. 2026/007
publicationDetails.journalName: MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
In May 2026, the MIT Humanitarian Supply Chain Lab within the MIT Center for Transportation & Logistics partnered with the National Institute of Building Sciences (NIBS) to convene a roundtable on delivering resilient housing solutions after disasters. The roundtable brought together representatives from public agencies, insurance, homebuilding, industrialized construction, standards organizations, community development, nonprofit recovery, finance, design, resilient building, and research.

The event was held under the Chatham House Rule to support candor and was structured around three goals: 1) identifying approaches to deliver rapidly deployable, cost-effective, and resilient housing after disasters; 2) exploring how communities can shape demand to meet survivor needs and accelerate construction industry transformation; and 3) identifying policy and operational friction that slows the survivor journey back home. The discussion focused more on single-family homes than multi-family or rental housing.

title: Industrial Policy and Short-Run Distributional Effects

detail.title: Industrial Policy and Short-Run Distributional Effects
detail.abstract:
This paper studies the short-run distributional effects of industrial policy. In the model, sectors differ in their external economies of scale. The policy subsidizes employment in high-externality sectors and taxes employment in low-externality sectors.

While such a policy reallocates resources and raises welfare in the long run, its short-run effects can be very different when workers cannot move across sectors. In the immediate short run, sectoral employment remains fixed, so the policy affects sectoral wages: wages rise in subsidized sectors and fall in taxed sectors. I derive an expression for welfare changes across worker groups and show that groups gain more when their initial employment is concentrated in high-externality sectors.

I quantify this mechanism for the United States by treating commuting zones as worker groups. I combine commuting-zone employment data with sector-level estimates of external scale elasticities from Bartelme, Costinot, Donaldson, and Rodriguez-Clare (2025). The results show substantial geographic heterogeneity: about 60 percent of commuting zones gain in the short run, while about 40 percent lose. Gains are concentrated mainly east of the Great Plains region, reflecting the geography of manufacturing employment.

title: The Procured Rule: Government AI, Private Nondelegation, and Public Power by Contract

detail.title: The Procured Rule: Government AI, Private Nondelegation, and Public Power by Contract
detail.abstract: In late 2025 the federal government began fixing the operative behavior of the artificial-intelligence systems it uses through the terms on which it buys them. Executive guidance now makes it a material condition of acquisition, enforceable by termination, that a procured large language model document its acceptable-use policy, disclose features of its configuration, and satisfy substantive constraints on what it may say. The reflexive worry is that this delegates public power to private firms and that the private nondelegation doctrine should reach it. The doctrine supplies no satisfactory answer, and FCC v. Consumers' Research shows why it is an unstable and incomplete tool: it asks whether the government retained control, a question procurement appears to answer for the government while the operative rule sits in a configuration the buyer cannot inspect, alter, or freeze. That procurement can carry privately designed policy into government, and can do so outside the ordinary channels of administrative process, is a recognized problem. This essay isolates within it a particular legal object. A procured rule is an operative rule of governmental decision that takes effect through a purchase and materially conditions a class of consequential determinations, and it comes in two forms: an inherited rule, the vendor's proprietary configuration entering with the product, limited by opacity and decisional dependence; and an imposed rule, the government's own behavioral requirements written into the contract rather than promulgated, limited by substantive decisional effect and, in its leading instance, set to expire on a fixed sunset. The reversal that gives the phenomenon its edge is that the same contract terms scholarship has proposed as the remedy for algorithmic accountability can themselves become the source of a substantive governmental rule that never acquires public-law status. The problem is not that the configuration is unseen; years of scholarship have seen it, and procurement policy has now made it an object of governance. It is that the procured rule has operative force without public-law status, generating internal records but no guaranteed public one, no contestation available to the governed, and content reversible with an administration. The remedy is to give what procurement already produces that status, through the acquisition system's own rulemaking and the ordinary law of administrative records, rather than through the constitutional law of delegation.

title: Allocative Creativity: A Model of Human-AI Creative Work in Organizations
affiliations: Brandeis University - International Business School and Brandeis University - International Business School

detail.title: Allocative Creativity: A Model of Human-AI Creative Work in Organizations
detail.abstract: Creativity has always been a human trait. For decades, theories of organizational creativity assumed that a single human mind performs the integrative act, the moment when knowledge, process, and motivation come together to produce creative output. Generative AI breaks this assumption. AI now works as a creative agent of its own, and the integrative act no longer sits inside one human mind. It splits across the human and the machine. This split forces us to rethink how organizations theorize creativity and innovation. Since existing frameworks are anchored in human-centric assumptions, they lack the conceptual vocabulary to explain how creative agency is distributed between human and machine. To address this theoretical gap, we propose the Allocative Creativity Model. The model treats human-machine creative work as one phenomenon. It runs across two levels, work and organizational, and three dynamics hold it together (configuration constraint, homogenization feedback, and identity-allocation co-evolution). The model rests on two new constructs. The first is the allocative decision, the choice of who does what, which we treat as a creative act in its own right. The second is allocative culture, a new dimension of an organization's creative identity.

title: A Participation Calibrated Gamma Exposure Methodology for Index Options

detail.title: A Participation Calibrated Gamma Exposure Methodology for Index Options
detail.abstract:
Gamma Exposure (GEX) is widely used to characterise option-market positioning, estimate dealer hedging pressure, and identify potential gamma-regime boundaries. As described in Section 4, the conventional framework aggregates option gamma using open interest and contract size while assigning a fixed positive contribution to calls and a fixed negative contribution to puts. This construction provides a tractable proxy for aggregate dealer positioning but implicitly relies on a stable relationship between option type and the sign of the passive book's inventory, an assumption that may not hold in structurally heterogeneous options markets such as India.

Section 3 establishes the mathematical foundations for option gamma and implied volatility, while Section 5 develops the proposed Participation-Calibrated Gamma Exposure (PC-GEX) methodology to relax the fixed-sign assumption. PC-GEX infers the likely sign of passive gamma inventory from three jointly observable market signals: footprint order-flow direction, changes in open interest (ΔOI), and changes in implied volatility (ΔIV). These signals provide complementary information on trade aggressor direction, position formation or unwinding, and the option-demand component of price changes, allowing the methodology to distinguish inventory accumulation from position reduction without requiring direct observation of dealer books.

The proposed framework further formalises this inference through an eight-case decision matrix and a cumulative inventory approach that assigns a GEX increment to each strike and observation interval before aggregating exposure across active strikes. The resulting PC-GEX measure therefore represents accumulated passive-book gamma conditioned on observed market activity rather than on a predetermined option-type sign convention. The mathematical formulation, including the GEX increment, cumulative strike-level exposure, and aggregate PC-GEX measure, is presented in the proposed methodology section. Empirical validation against conventional signed-OI GEX, using return autocorrelation and expiry-pinning distance as evaluation criteria, is reserved for subsequent work following systematic data collection and backtesting.

title: From Indicators to Policy Feedback: Evidence-Informed Evaluation of Regional Development
affiliations: MGIMO University

detail.title: From Indicators to Policy Feedback: Evidence-Informed Evaluation of Regional Development
detail.abstract: Administrative data and econometric tools have not eliminated the political problem of evaluation: indicators can inform a decision, but they cannot determine public goals, legitimate distributional choices, or responsibility on their own. This paper develops an evidenceinformed feedback framework for Russian regional policy. The empirical component uses 24 observations for Tula Region, Primorsky Territory, the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia), and Sakhalin Region in 2019-2024. Gross regional product is related to investment, industrial production, construction, wages, and unemployment through pooled regression, HC3 robust inference, and regional fixed effects.
