Investment retains a positive association with GRP and unemployment a negative one; construction and wages are specification-sensitive, while industrial production provides no stable signal. The findings are interpreted as diagnostics rather than causal programme effects because the sample is small, monetary variables are measured at current prices, and lags and reverse causality remain. The paper proposes three feedback loops: administrative control of resources and outputs, statistical assessment of social and territorial outcomes, and political review through explanation, participation, and a binding decision to continue, modify, redistribute, or terminate an instrument. Econometric evidence becomes useful when embedded in an accountable procedure capable of learning from divergence among expenditure, facility completion, employment, and territorial effects.

title: A Comparative Analysis of American and Iranian Political Systems and Their Impact on the Iran-U.S.-Israel Triangle War

detail.title: A Comparative Analysis of American and Iranian Political Systems and Their Impact on the Iran-U.S.-Israel Triangle War

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal or financial relationships with any person or organization that could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patients, or primary data collection. The analysis relies exclusively on publicly available official statements, news reporting, and published think-tank commentary; no ethics approval was therefore required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or funding from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This article extends Robert Putnam's two-level game framework to analyze how domestic political institutions in the United States, Iran, and Israel shaped the onset, escalation, and partial de-escalation of the 2024-2026 Iran-U.S.-Israel conflict. The analysis is explicitly time-stamped: it covers events through early August 2026, and several of the developments it discusses-most importantly the status of the Strait of Hormuz and the durability of the June 2026 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)-remain unresolved as of this writing. Rather than treating the war as a closed historical episode, the article maps Level I international bargaining against Level II domestic ratification constraints across five critical episodes: the 2024 Iranian missile barrages, the June 2025 U.S./Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear and military infrastructure, the February-April 2026 escalation culminating in the February 28, 2026 U.S.-Israeli decapitation strike that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and several senior commanders, the April-June 2026 ceasefire-and-negotiation sequence that produced the Islamabad MoU, and the contested implementation period that has followed. Through process-tracing of open-source evidence, the study finds that U.S. win-sets contracted and expanded in a pattern only partially explained by electoral proximity; Iranian Level II constraints-dominated by regime-survival imperatives and reinforced, rather than disrupted, by the assassination of the Supreme Leader and the succession of Mojtaba Khamenei-produced narrow concessions on core "resistance" issues alongside high tolerance for proxy and economic costs; and Israeli coalition-security dynamics generated expansive win-sets for kinetic operations, punctuated by at least one notable instance of externally induced restraint. The analysis engages realist, bureaucratic, audience-cost, and constructivist alternatives on a case-by-case basis, conceding specific points to each rather than claiming uniform subsumption. It closes with contingency-based policy implications and an explicit statement of the analysis's provisional status. Readers encountering this abstract in isolation (e.g., via a database record) should treat the piece as explicitly time-stamped and provisional, current as of early August 2026, rather than as a completed retrospective.

title: UETHA (Universal Economic Theory of Human Action): A Diagnostic Framework for Assessing Economic Schools

detail.title: UETHA (Universal Economic Theory of Human Action): A Diagnostic Framework for Assessing Economic Schools
detail.abstract: This paper examines two important problems in economics: the fragmentation of economic thought and the absence of a comprehensive definition and standard diagnostic tool for evaluating economic schools and policies. Many existing tools do not provide a unified framework that connects individual economic behavior (micro level) with the needs of society as a whole (macro level). Because of this limitation, many ineffective or fundamentally flawed policies have remained in use for long periods during the last 400 years. To address this issue, the study introduces UETHA (Universal Economic Theory of Human Action), a two-tier diagnostic framework for evaluating economic systems. The model uses two main filters: principled alignment, which examines whether a system is consistent with individual economic principles and the resulting cost-benefit algorithm, and structural coherence, which evaluates the key pillars of the collective economy: specialization, exchange, and taxation. The findings indicate that economic systems are most resilient and efficient when they operate within a defined "maintenance corridor." In this setting, the government functions as an institutional maintenance expert rather than as a direct market actor. By applying this framework to major schools of economics, the study demonstrates its value as an "early warning system" for assessing economic schools and policies. It also highlights the potential of UETHA to become an important analytical framework in economics.

title: Retirement Precursor Variables: Regression Analysis (Evidence from PSID)
affiliations: University of Houston and University of Houston

detail.title: Retirement Precursor Variables: Regression Analysis (Evidence from PSID)
detail.abstract: This study is a partial dive into and testing of variables that have the potential to be identified as precursors to the decision to save in or withdraw from retirement accounts. For now, we focused on 5 variables: Age, Gender, Total Income, Health, and Saving Rate. We sourced data from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID) and transformed the data in two ways. One, we created the savings rate column by using existing IRA income and total taxable income from the survey per individual. Second, we transformed the health responses into unique aggregate scores based on household size and the proportion of the family that reported far-from-average health circumstances (which we transformed into a binary variable). Using the data, we tested two models, with the difference between the two being that one included savings rate and one didn't. To put it simply, we found that the models displayed R-squared scores of .39 and .40. In the end, we note that people tend not to withdraw funds as much when they aren't subject to high financial health burdens and withdraw more when they are. Other than that, the data fits the empirical consensus that people tend to spend more as they age due to the lack of commitment devices in the form of tax penalties for retirement accounts, along with the life cycle hypothesis.

title: Stakeholder Comments on the Draft Intellectual Property (Enforcement & Coordination) Rules, 2025
affiliations: and Fatima Jinnah Women University

detail.title: Stakeholder Comments on the Draft Intellectual Property (Enforcement & Coordination) Rules, 2025
detail.abstract: This paper presents a critical legal and policy analysis of the Draft Intellectual Property (Enforcement & Coordination) Rules, 2026, examining their proposed enforcement mechanisms, institutional coordination framework, and implications for effective IP protection in Pakistan. The analysis identifies key legal, procedural, and institutional issues and proposes recommendations aimed at strengthening coherence, accountability, and practical enforceability. The comments were formally submitted to IPO Pakistan as part of its stakeholder consultation process

title: Runtime Legitimacy in ICT Supply Chains: A Three-Layer Framework for Cybersecurity Governance under Sanctions in Iran
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Runtime Legitimacy in ICT Supply Chains: A Three-Layer Framework for Cybersecurity Governance under Sanctions in Iran
detail.abstract:
This paper extends the Runtime Legitimacy framework, originally developed to evaluate the legitimacy of autonomous AI decisions at the moment of execution, to the domain of ICT supply chain security. It argues that Iran's existing legal framework addresses cyberattacks mainly after the fact, while today's risks, amplified by sanctions and constrained procurement channels, take shape earlier, at the design and procurement stages of equipment.

To test this hypothesis, the paper analyzes the legitimacy of ICT equipment across three distinct but interlocking layers: design-time legitimacy, procurement-time legitimacy, and runtime legitimacy. The central argument is that the legitimacy of a piece of equipment is the product of these three components, not their sum; a weakness in any single layer can void the entire chain of trust, even if the other two layers remain sound.

Using this three-layer framework, the paper identifies four specific legal gaps in Iran's current regime: the absence of a pre-import security assessment mechanism, ambiguity in the distribution of liability among manufacturers, intermediaries, importers, and operators, the absence of a national standard for Firmware and Hardware security assessment, and the absence of independent laboratories with judicial standing. For each gap, the Runtime Legitimacy for ICT Supply Chains model offers a specific technical and institutional response.

Drawing on a comparative study of European Union regulation (the NIS2 Directive and the Cyber Resilience Act) and United States regulation (Executive Order 14028), the paper proposes two legislative paths: adding a defined chapter to the Computer Crimes Law as a fast-track measure, and drafting a standalone ICT supply chain security law as a medium-term horizon. The paper concludes that shifting from post-attack response to preventive supply chain governance is the most urgent reform Iranian cyber law currently needs.

title: The Predatory Tax: Residual Targeting and the Timing of Public Transfers
affiliations: and Shanghai Lixin University of Accounting and Finance

detail.title: The Predatory Tax: Residual Targeting and the Timing of Public Transfers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicted interests within the scope of this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval statement is not applicable to this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research is currently not funded by any affiliations.

detail.abstract: Public-transfer analysis usually treats the recipient as the terminal private claimant: once a payment is delivered, subsequent allocation is modeled as household choice. This paper studies a downstream market in which private predators acquire an endogenous claim on transferred resources. Formal-market exclusion raises willingness to pay for false re-entry into employment, status, security, or institutional membership, while prior extraction lowers the liquidity that remains capturable. Their single crossing generates residual targeting: predatory profit is maximized among households whose outside options have deteriorated but whose resources are not yet exhausted. A message-design extension separates prestigious association from auditable guarantee and shows why low-verification markets receive high-prestige, lowguarantee claims. For public transfers, I decompose equal-present-value payment paths into pledgeable liquidity and a protected future floor. A protected installment stream reduces predatory loss through both a liquidity channel and an outside-option channel; the shield vanishes exactly when future payments become fully pledgeable. The model yields a marginal predatory tax, a schedule effect on net loss, and a sufficient-statistic condition under which capture reverses the conventional welfare ranking of lump sums and installments. The paper then establishes the design required to identify these objects and audits the public replication files of a canonical Kenyan cash-transfer experiment. Two published timing resultsfor assets and food security-reproduce exactly, but no event-level measure of fraud, bribery, extortion, or related net loss exists. Standard household outcomes therefore identify the familiar investment-smoothing tradeoff while leaving downstream capture unidentified. Payment form determines not only when assistance can be spent, but potentially who ultimately captures it.

title: Scaling Carbon Removal: From Pilot Plants to Planetary Impact

detail.title: Scaling Carbon Removal: From Pilot Plants to Planetary Impact
detail.abstract: Climate commentary treats direct air capture, enhanced weathering, and biochar as three co-equal carbon-removal technologies racing down a single cost curve toward gigatonne scale. The public files treat them as three different objects. Novel carbon dioxide removal was 2.04 million tonnes in 2025 in the State of Carbon Dioxide Removal, 3rd Edition. Biochar was 1.46 million tonnes of that total. Verified enhanced weathering was 0.0038 million tonnes. Verified direct air capture with storage was 0.0015 million tonnes. Conventional removal from afforestation and reforestation averaged 2,200 million tonnes a year over 2014-23. Fossil carbon dioxide was 38.6 billion tonnes in 2024. The 2030 pipeline of projects operating or under construction is 8.4 million tonnes, 0.24 percent of the 3.5 billion tonnes of novel removal that 1.5°C scenarios need by 2050. We score 213 countries on three binary clocks. DAC-ready: electricity access of at least 90 percent, generation of at least 2,000 kilowatt-hours per person, and either solar-plus-wind at 8 percent of generation or a low-carbon share of 40 percent. Enhanced-weathering-ready: at least 2 million hectares of arable land, fertilizer use of at least 50 kilograms per hectare, and cereal yields of at least 2,000 kilograms per hectare. Biochar-ready: a material cereal or forest residue stream plus an agricultural sector that can take an amendment. Seventy-one countries close the DAC clock, covering 3.31 billion people. Forty-five close the weathering clock, covering 5.87 billion. Ninety close the biochar clock, covering 7.46 billion. Twenty-seven countries close all three. India closes weathering and biochar and fails DAC, at 1,418 kilowatt-hours and 154 million hectares of cropland. Iceland closes DAC and fails the field, at 49,730 kilowatt-hours and 0.1 million hectares. A dollar ranking that puts weathering below DAC and DAC on a path to $100 per tonne does not describe this map. DAC is an energy-and-storage plant. Weathering is a mill, a field, and a verification lag. Biochar is a residue stream. Rank the stocks first.

title: Hedge and Seek: A Q-Learning Approach to Dynamic Hedging of the S&P 500 and Gold with Futures
affiliations: Iowa State University

detail.title: Hedge and Seek: A Q-Learning Approach to Dynamic Hedging of the S&P 500 and Gold with Futures
detail.abstract: This paper develops a reinforcement learning framework based on CARA utility to dynamically determine hedge ratios for S&P 500 index exposure using E-mini S&P 500 futures contracts and gold exposure using gold futures contracts. Using Q-learning combined with an XGBoost model over a comprehensive state space spanning 2007-2022, the proposed framework outperforms standard hedging benchmarks (such as the Minimum Variance) across Sharpe and Information ratios, Maximum Drawdown, and Certainty Equivalent. To provide economic interpretability, I combine SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature attribution with Principal Component and Time-Series regression analysis. Results indicate that credit conditions, inflation, monetary policy, and the yield curve play important roles in hedge decisions. The RL strategy performs particularly well during structural changes, but its flexibility offers less advantage in stable and slowly evolving regimes. Additionally, its performance depends on the analyzed markets, sample period, and modeling choices, highlighting the importance of further evaluation across alternative environments and implementations.

title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals
affiliations: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI) - Lally School of Management and University of Maryland, College Park

detail.title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals

declarations.funderStatement: We are thankful to the University of Maryland for the generous funding for data acquisition.

detail.abstract: We study California's short-term lodging price transparency law (AB 537), which from July 1, 2024 required Airbnb and other providers to advertise fee-inclusive prices. Using Coarsened Exact Matching to compare Airbnb listings in San Diego and San Francisco with those in Seattle and Chicago, we find that all-in pricing made guests more price-sensitive relative to control cities; yet, contrary to the standard prediction that transparency lowers prices, average daily rates rose by 4.8 percent. We also observe significant market churn: relative to control cities, treated cities saw more exits and entries, listings reliant on cleaning-fee revenue disproportionately exited, higher-quality listings were more likely to stay, and entrants offered lower fees and lower quality than incumbents. A discrete-choice welfare analysis shows that the law removed a sizable "welfare illusion" created by obscured fees and, largely through market churn, raised realized consumer surplus. The net gains, after accounting for price increases, were positive on average but unevenly distributed across treated ZIP codes.

title: Assessing the Impacts of Heatwaves and Floods on Maternal and Child Healthcare Utilisation: A Realist-Informed Systematic Review and Causal Loop Diagram
affiliations: , International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, University of Zambia (UNZA), University of Zambia (UNZA), African Institute for Development Policy, , , Universidade Estadual de Maringá,  Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS), State University of Maringá, London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, , London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, University of Zambia, Universidade de Brasília (UnB) and International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA)

detail.title: Assessing the Impacts of Heatwaves and Floods on Maternal and Child Healthcare Utilisation: A Realist-Informed Systematic Review and Causal Loop Diagram

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no competing interests. The authors alone are responsible for the views expressed in this article and they do not necessarily represent the views of the organisations listed.
declarations.funderStatement: This research is part of the REACH project (Building resilience to floods and heat in the maternal and child health system in Brazil and Zambia), funded by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) and the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC [Grant Number: ES/Y00258X/1]. The funders had no role in the study design; data collection, analysis, or interpretation; manuscript preparation; or the decision to submit the article for publication.

detail.abstract: Heatwaves and floods are increasing globally, posing growing risks to health systems and disrupting maternal and child health (MCH) service utilisation. Understanding whether, how, and in which contexts these hazards affect MCH care is essential for effective adaptation planning. We conducted a realist-informed systematic review across seven databases, identifying 5,280 records. After dual screening, 36 studies met the inclusion criteria, reporting the effects of floods and/or heatwaves on routine and emergency MCH service utilisation (23 floods, 12 heatwaves, and 1 both). No restrictions were applied by language, setting, or study design. Findings were synthesised narratively, and a causal loop diagram was developed to represent underlying pathways. Heatwaves and floods disrupted MCH service utilisation through six mechanisms: restricted travel, population displacement, income loss, increased health risks, health service disruption, and general infrastructure disruption. Evidence on heatwaves was strongest for emergency and inpatient care, including maternal hospitalisations, obstetric emergencies, neonatal intensive care admissions, and under-five emergency department visits, while evidence on routine care was very limited. In contrast, floods were associated with reduced routine service use, including antenatal care, institutional delivery, and postnatal care, and impeded access to emergency obstetric care, contributing to delayed referrals and preventable deaths. Floods and heatwaves affect MCH service utilisation through shared and hazard-specific pathways shaped by contextual vulnerability. Key evidence gaps include limited qualitative evidence on heatwaves, scarce research on child health services beyond acute care, and uneven geographic coverage. These findings can inform targeted strategies to strengthen climate-resilient MCH systems.

title:
Mechanism-informed Inference Models  
A Category, and Its Scope Conditions

detail.title:
Mechanism-informed Inference Models  
A Category, and Its Scope Conditions
detail.abstract: Physics-informed machine learning has established that encoding known scientific structure into a learning problem improves data efficiency and extrapolation. This paper argues that the operative property is not that the structure is physical, but that it is explicit, inspectable, and parameterized by quantities with meaning. We name the resulting class Mechanism-Informed Inference Models (MIIM), of which physics-informed approaches are the special case in which the mechanism is physical law. We distinguish MIIM from physics-informed neural networks, which are predominantly solvers and surrogates, and from physics-informed inference more narrowly construed. We state three scope conditions under which the class applies-nonobservability of the target, expressibility of the mechanism, and identifiability of its parameters from realistically attainable data-and argue that the third is routinely violated in practice and rarely tested. We propose that calibration of stated uncertainty and detection of structural misspecification, rather than point accuracy, are the appropriate evaluation criteria for the class, and distinguish the legitimate distillation of a mechanism into a surrogate from the distillation of an inference, which does not preserve the calibration guarantee. A worked pharmacokinetic example is given, and a negative example is given in which a well-converged fit produced a substantially incorrect answer because a scope condition failed. This is a position paper; it does not propose a new estimator.

title: Tambora Eruption and Peasant Revolts in Qing China: An Apocalypse
affiliations: Nanjing University - Department of Economics, Fudan University - Department of Economics and Xiamen University - Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE)

detail.title: Tambora Eruption and Peasant Revolts in Qing China: An Apocalypse
detail.abstract: The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia was the deadliest volcanic eruption in recorded human history. Massive amounts of sulfur-rich aerosols were ejected into the atmosphere, blocking solar radiation and triggering global temperature declines. We exploit this unique natural experiment to identify two pathways through which climate disasters affect social stability. Using prefecture-level data from the Qing Dynasty of China, we show that a one-standard-deviation increase in crop heat requirements is associated with 2.256 additional revolts per million residents, equivalent to 0.184 standard deviations of the outcome. Consistent with prior literature, we show that the cooling-induced crop failure raised grain prices, a channel long linked to social instability. Furthermore, we quantify a belief-coordination channel. The Tambora-affected regions also witnessed a significant rise in recorded activity of the White Lotus, the largest millenarian sect in Qing China mobilizing peasant revolts against the emperor. Our study provides historical evidence to highlight the underappreciated social risks that extreme climate shocks pose today.

title: From Rhetoric to Strategic Survival: The Decline of Mohajir Politics and Deng Xiaoping's Strategic Lesson
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: From Rhetoric to Strategic Survival: The Decline of Mohajir Politics and Deng Xiaoping's Strategic Lesson
detail.abstract:
This paper presents a critical political-economic analysis of the structural decline of the Urdu-speaking Mohajir community in urban Sindh, Pakistan, while offering a strategic framework for socio-economic revitalization modeled after Deng Xiaoping’s pragmatic governance model. Historically characterized by intellectual, educational, and institutional dominance, urban Mohajir politics over the past four decades became severely compromised through militarized street-level mobilization, extreme factionalism, personality cults, and reliance on state establishment patronage. This study evaluates how the transition from institutional leadership to militant rhetoric resulted in economic destabilization, political isolation, and capital flight from key urban powerhouses like Karachi and Hyderabad.

Drawing a comparative lens to post-1989 Chinese strategic recalibration, the paper argues that the survival and long-term prosperity of urban Sindh's populace lies in adopting Deng’s doctrine of "Tao Guang Yang Hui" (hide your strength, bide your time). The author formulates a four-pillar framework centered on: (1) political de-escalation and quiet internal capacity building, (2) transition from street dominance to technological and educational competitiveness, (3) economic integration with regional majority demographics, and (4) strict pragmatic development over dogmatic identity politics. Ultimately, the paper provides a policy-oriented blueprint for transforming an ethnically polarized urban demographic into an indispensable global technological and economic hub.

title: Netting Without a Declaration: Saldirovanie, Retrospectivity and the Insolvency Estate in Russian Construction Contracts
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Netting Without a Declaration: Saldirovanie, Retrospectivity and the Insolvency Estate in Russian Construction Contracts
detail.abstract: Russian law has developed, over roughly the last eight years, a mechanism for reconciling mutual performances under a terminated contract that operates without any declaration, without a counterclaim, and without the possibility of avoidance in insolvency. It is called saldirovanie — the determination of the completion obligation (завершающая обязанность) of one party towards the other. It is not set-off. It is not a transaction. On the current understanding it is not an act of will at all, but an arithmetical consequence of what the parties in fact rendered to each other. On 2 December 2025 the Chamber for Commercial Disputes of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation gave that mechanism a temporal dimension that had not previously been settled. In Tekhmontazh v Committee for Construction of St Petersburg the Chamber held that where the parties have not agreed on the completion obligation and the matter falls to be resolved by a court, judicial netting operates retrospectively to the date of contract termination, irrespective of when the court confirmed it. A contractual penalty payable on breach of a reciprocal obligation does not stand outside the principal debt but alters its size: the contractor's breach reduces the employer's payment debt by the amount of the penalty due to the employer, while the employer's breach generates additional payments over and above the contract price. The consequence is that default interest claimed by the contractor for late payment must be calculated on the netted figure, backdated by eight years, rather than on the gross sum recorded in the accounts at the time. This paper examines the holding against the English treatment of the same problem — the accrual of liquidated damages up to termination, restated by the UK Supreme Court in Triple Point Technology Inc v PTT Public Company Ltd — and argues that the outcomes converge while the mechanisms diverge sharply. English law keeps the liquidated sum as a distinct right that must be asserted; Russian law folds it into the principal debt, so that the party against whom it operates must displace it rather than the party in whose favour it operates assert it. The paper then identifies a problem the judgment does not address. The contractor in Tekhmontazh was in liquidation, and the netting had been carried out in its own insolvency proceedings. Retrospectivity means that the institution operates against the insolvency estate twice over: once by reducing the claim against the employer, and again by shrinking the base on which the estate's own penalty claim is computed. The economic logic of reciprocal performance and the insolvency logic of ranking and creditor equality collide, and the collision is not discussed.

title: Advanced Insurance Analytics for Fraud Prevention

detail.title: Advanced Insurance Analytics for Fraud Prevention
detail.abstract: Insurance fraud is a rapidly evolving threat to the U.S. insurance industry, generating substantial economic losses and increasing operational, regulatory, and reputational risks. This paper examines six priority fraud vectors reshaping the insurance landscape: generative artificial intelligence and deepfake fraud, organized fraud rings, catastrophe-related fraud, healthcare and medical billing fraud, cyber-insurance fraud, and vendor and third-party fraud. It evaluates the analytical technologies, data-governance practices, investigative tools, and operational controls insurers are deploying to detect and mitigate these risks. The paper also considers emerging regulatory expectations, including the National Association of Insurance Commissioners' guidance on artificial intelligence and the Insurance Fraud Prevention Model Act. Drawing on industry practices, the paper proposes practical, risk-based strategies for strengthening fraud detection, investigation, governance, and prevention. The analysis demonstrates that effective insurance fraud prevention requires an integrated framework combining advanced analytics, human oversight, cross-sector information sharing, and robust AI and third-party governance.

title: New Evidence on the Macroeconomic Effects of Carbon Taxes
affiliations: Rochester Institute of Technology

detail.title: New Evidence on the Macroeconomic Effects of Carbon Taxes
detail.abstract: This short paper examines evidence that effective carbon taxes reduce greenhouse gas emissions but also lower gross domestic product (GDP) and increase unemployment, highlighting macroeconomic tradeoffs and the importance of revenue recycling and complementary climate policies.

title: Exact Tail Dependence Coefficients for Archimedean Copulas: Derivation of Asymptotic Multivariate Dependence Formulas

detail.title: Exact Tail Dependence Coefficients for Archimedean Copulas: Derivation of Asymptotic Multivariate Dependence Formulas
detail.abstract: We derive bivariate and multivariate tail-dependence coefficients for Archimedean copulas and introduce a signed stress-concordance diagnostic for Colombian financial loss vectors. The contribution is analytical: closed-form tail formulas are paired with an economically oriented interpretation for currency, equity, commodity, and sovereign-risk co-movements.

title: Beyond Greenwashing: Algorithmic Resilience and the Non-Linear Governance Premium in Sovereign Capital Flows
affiliations: and Rennes School of Business

detail.title: Beyond Greenwashing: Algorithmic Resilience and the Non-Linear Governance Premium in Sovereign Capital Flows
detail.abstract: Despite the proliferation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) metrics, traditional linear macro-financial models frequently fail to capture the complex, non-linear transmission mechanisms driving Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows during systemic shocks. To address this methodological gap, this paper introduces a machine learning architecture optimised via a Bayesian hyperparameter tournament, employing a rigorous forward-chaining panel split to eliminate temporal data leakage across a global dataset of 147 sovereign entities from 2010 to 2024. Out-of-sample evaluations, formally validated via two-sided modified Diebold-Mariano testing, reveal that an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) ensemble emerges as the optimal predictive engine. It demonstrates statistically significant superiority over L1-regularised Lasso baselines and continuous non-linear estimators (p < 0.05). Regime-specific residual analysis demonstrates a profound asymmetric advantage: the XGBoost architecture achieves its greatest predictive alpha by dynamically compressing forecast errors by nearly 36% against linear baselines during extreme macroeconomic tail events. By integrating dual Explainable AI frameworks (SHAP and LIME) empirically validated for methodological consensus via Spearman rank correlation (p < 0.001), this study mathematically maps the non-linear threshold effects of institutional quality, confirming a strict "Governance Premium" dictating capital flows. Finally, the deployment of Mondrian split-conformal prediction establishes dynamic, regime-conditional 95% marginal coverage bounds that exhibit structural "graceful degradation," successfully retaining reliable safety nets even under severe adversarial data corruption. This framework provides policymakers with an empirically robust, distribution-agnostic tool for quantifying sovereign tail-risk uncertainty.

title: From Burnout to Retention: Five Policy Recommendations for Public School Teachers in Punjab, Pakistan, Using the Job Demands-resources Model
affiliations: The Smart School

detail.title: From Burnout to Retention: Five Policy Recommendations for Public School Teachers in Punjab, Pakistan, Using the Job Demands-resources Model
detail.abstract: Teacher turnover in public schools of Punjab, Pakistan poses a significant challenge to education quality and government expenditure. Data from the School Education Department shows a net decline of 45,958 teachers from 2020-2024 alongside a 25% vacancy rate, indicating persistent retention pressures. While international literature extensively uses the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model to explain teacher burnout and retention, there is a gap in applying this framework to develop concrete policy recommendations for the Pakistani context. Recent pay revisions in July 2026 were offset by 26.0% inflation in the prior fiscal year. This conceptual paper addresses that gap by analyzing systemic challenges in Punjab's public schools through the JD-R lens. Drawing on government reports and existing literature, the paper identifies key job demands-including assessment pressure, compensation concerns, and transfer-related insecurity-and resource deficits such as limited administrative support and limited career progression. Building on this analysis, the paper proposes five evidence-based policy recommendations: reducing assessment demands, introducing retention allowances, establishing school-based mentorship, creating a clear career ladder, and implementing a workload and wellbeing policy. Each recommendation is specified with a lead implementing department, an author-assessed implementation complexity, and a proposed timeline, to move the agenda from a policy headline toward an actionable proposal. The study contributes to theory by contextualizing the JD-R model for Pakistan and provides a practical five-point agenda for policymakers. This is a conceptual paper; several specific claims flagged in Section 3 require primary-source verification, and costing of the fiscal recommendations remains outstanding.

title: Algorithmic Decoupling and Supply Chain Contagion: Quantifying the Extraterritorial Impact of State Climate Mandates
affiliations: and Rennes School of Business

detail.title: Algorithmic Decoupling and Supply Chain Contagion: Quantifying the Extraterritorial Impact of State Climate Mandates
detail.abstract: Can localized climate regulations discipline a global corporate ecosystem? Exploiting the legislative shock of California SB 253, this paper investigates the extraterritorial impact of state-level Scope 3 emission mandates on systemic corporate greenwashing. We employ a novel Explainable AI (XAI) Natural Language Processing architecture, combining TF-IDF vectorization and CorEx topic modeling, to rigorously quantify the linguistic decoupling between climate rhetoric and substantive risk management. Analysing a longitudinal panel of 1,089 SEC 10-K filings, the baseline Two-Way Fixed Effects (TWFE) Difference-in-Differences estimation initially yields a statistically null interaction effect. However, isolating and analysing the temporal fixed effects reveals a profound, market-wide structural reduction in linguistic decoupling, thereby diagnosing a systematic violation of the Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption (SUTVA). We causally identify this convergence as "supply-chain contagion." Non-mandated mid-cap entities were economically compelled to systematically restructure their risk disclosures to satisfy the downstream Scope 3 procurement demands of their mandated mega-cap enterprise clients. Crucially, by deploying a dynamic event-study specification, we isolate a one-year structural transmission lag—mathematically mapping the exact operational timeline required for apex firms to translate internal compliance into external Business-to-Business (B2B) vendor enforcement. We isolate this state-specific contagion from concurrent Federal SEC rulemaking using a raw-text lexical falsification audit, and establish the statistical superiority of our deterministic methodology over probabilistic Large Language Model (LLM) benchmarks. Ultimately, we provide empirical proof that corporate supply-chain linkages act as highly efficient, invisible regulatory proxies, enforcing climate compliance deep into the global middle market.

title: Can an Indian Citizen Really Erase Their Digital Past? The Unfinished Right to be Forgotten in India
affiliations: Rajasthan High Court

detail.title: Can an Indian Citizen Really Erase Their Digital Past? The Unfinished Right to be Forgotten in India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a doctrinal and comparative legal analysis based on publicly available judgments, statutes, and secondary sources. It does not involve human participants or primary data collection requiring ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The right to be forgotten — the claim that individuals should, in defined circumstances, be able to have outdated or irrelevant personal information de-indexed or erased from public digital availability — remains incomplete and fragmented in Indian law. While the Supreme Court’s recognition of informational privacy in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) provides a constitutional foundation, the doctrine has developed almost entirely through inconsistent High Court decisions. Different High Courts have reached opposite conclusions on comparable facts, and even the most ambitious attempt to systematise the right — the Delhi High Court’s 2026 decision in Laksh Vir Singh Yadav — remains under appeal and limited in its territorial reach.

The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 offers only a narrow right to erasure, confined largely to data processed on the basis of consent and expressly excluding publicly available material such as court judgments and news archives — precisely the category of information most frequently at issue in Indian cases. As a result, litigants seeking de-indexing of old judicial records or news reports must continue to rely on uncodified, judge-made privacy jurisprudence rather than any coherent statutory framework.

This paper traces the conceptual origins of the right in the CJEU’s Google Spain decision, maps its uneven judicial development in India, critically assesses the limited contribution of the DPDP Act, and situates the Indian position against comparative models from the European Union, the United States, and the United Kingdom. It argues that India currently possesses only a provisional and geographically fragmented version of the right, and proposes a reform agenda centred on authoritative Supreme Court guidelines, a clearer distinction between private individuals and public figures, time-sensitive application, and targeted legislative clarification.

title: The Price of Greenwashing: Algorithmic Verification and Market Discipline using Conformal Machine Learning
affiliations: and Rennes School of Business

detail.title: The Price of Greenwashing: Algorithmic Verification and Market Discipline using Conformal Machine Learning
detail.abstract: While corporate sustainability mandates are expanding, the systemic reliance on self-reported emissions data exposes financial markets to pervasive greenwashing. Current literature predominantly utilizes subjective commercial ESG ratings or textual sentiment analysis to detect this deception, leaving a critical econometric gap in objectively quantifying physical climate realities. To resolve this information asymmetry, we engineer a novel algorithmic verification pipeline. Fusing U.S. SEC financial fundamentals with facility-level EPA greenhouse gas registries, we train a hyperparameter-optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) architecture to predict physical baseline emissions. To rigorously quantify epistemic uncertainty and account for extreme asset-class heteroskedasticity, we apply a Mondrian Conformal Prediction framework, generating mathematically guaranteed, firm-specific safety margins. The shortfall between self-reported emissions and this conformal baseline is standardized into a novel Conformal-Weighted Continuous Divergence (CWCD) metric. Utilizing a cross-sectional lead-lag econometric design with high-dimensional industry fixed effects, we evaluate the directional, leading predictive association of algorithmic divergence on subsequent market valuation (Tobin’s Q) and operational profitability (ROA). The empirical estimations reveal a robust predictive association indicative of market discipline: algorithmic emissions divergence exhibits a severe, statistically significant negative relationship with subsequent forward valuation and operational profitability. Providing robust evidence against the market blindness hypothesis, this study strongly suggests that institutional capital possesses the mechanisms to actively price environmental deception as a leading indicator of fundamental corporate mismanagement. These findings provide the quantitative justification necessary for regulatory authorities and asset managers to deploy algorithmic auditing infrastructure at scale.

title: Out-of-Sample Evaluation of an Intraday Momentum Strategy for the S&P 500 ETF (SPY)

detail.title: Out-of-Sample Evaluation of an Intraday Momentum Strategy for the S&P 500 ETF (SPY)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this study. The paper independently evaluates a strategy proposed by other authors; the author has no financial or professional relationship with them or with any organization connected to the work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study did not involve human participants, animals, or personal data; it uses only aggregated market price data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Zarattini, Aziz, and Barbon (2025) present an intraday momentum strategy for SPY that achieves an annualized return of 19.6% and a Sharpe Ratio of 1.33 over the period 2007-2024. This paper independently replicates their strategy using IQFeed 1-minute data and evaluates its performance on approximately two years of out-of-sample data (May 2024 to March 2026). Our in-sample replication closely matches the original results, confirming the reproducibility of the strategy (Sharpe Ratio 1.34 over 2015-2024). However, out-of-sample performance deteriorates substantially: the strategy achieves a total return of only 9.4% versus 29.5% for a passive buy-and-hold, with a Sharpe Ratio of 0.39. The decline in risk-adjusted returns is statistically significant. We examine potential explanations for this degradation, including changing market microstructure, the proliferation of zero-days-to-expiration (0-DTE) options, and the possibility that the observed underperformance falls within historical drawdown norms. Our findings highlight the importance of out-of-sample validation for intraday trading strategies and contribute to the ongoing discussion about the persistence of momentum anomalies at high frequencies.

title: Concession and Debt Recovery
affiliations: PBCSF, Tsinghua University, Hong Kong Polytechnic University - School of Accounting and Finance, Jinan University and The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Concession and Debt Recovery
detail.abstract: Performance varies widely across debt collectors. Using 100,000 recorded calls from a Chinese NPL platform, we parse the verbal content of each call and match it to follow-up repayment. On each call the collector offers a concession, threatens, or merely notifies. Relative to calls that merely notify, a concession raises the probability of future payment by 13 to 15 percentage points on the calls whose strategy the instrument shifts, and the total amount recovered per call by about $80. Threats show no causal effect in this deeply delinquent sample. The mechanism has two sides. The concession changes the borrower's willingness to engage and execute, not her ability to pay. The collector gauges that willingness and decides when to concede. She tends to concede too late, after the conversation has turned hostile, when concessions do the least. If collectors extended concessions promptly, recovery would rise by about 13 percent. The collector is an overlooked actor in the credit system. Simple interventions in the timing of concessions could substantially improve recovery on non-performing loans.

title: Taming the 50-Year Dragon: An Algorithmic Key Rate Duration Shield to Immunize a $1 Billion Nuclear SMR Project against Fed Rate Shocks
affiliations: Ain Shams University Cairo

detail.title: Taming the 50-Year Dragon: An Algorithmic Key Rate Duration Shield to Immunize a $1 Billion Nuclear SMR Project against Fed Rate Shocks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The transition of the United States energy sector toward complete decarbonization, coupled with continuous grid demand shocks, has positioned next-generation nuclear power as a critical national strategic asset. Among emerging clean energy baseload alternatives, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) offer an unparalleled technical utility due to their factory-fabricated, zero-emission configurations. However, deploying SMR technology is deeply constrained by financing friction; funding a single reactor requires an immense fixed initial capital outlay of $1 Billion CapEx amortized over an extended lifespan of 50 years.
Across this half-century horizon, the portfolio is heavily vulnerable to severe interest rate regime shifts executed during aggressive Federal Reserve monetary tightening cycles. These macroeconomic shocks induce non-parallel term structure transformations, such as Bearish Flattening vectors and yield inversions. Legacy public underwriting pipelines evaluate risk using a single-parameter index—Global Effective Duration—which blindly assumes parallel market movements. Because this global metric is blind to localized node variance along the time axis, traditional capital structures concentrate severe financial hazards at the terminal milestone where the return of the capital principal physically occurs. This single-parameter exposure leaves multi-decade public utility funding vulnerable to immediate debt inflation, dragging the portfolio into technical default zones and eroding taxpayer liquidity
This study resolves the funding crisis by introducing a re-engineered, multi-asset algorithmic framework—Model C—that bridges the academic silo between
banking risk models and public sector infrastructure debt engineering. Rather than relying on static global duration averages, the proposed engine integrates a high-dimensional Key Rate (KRD) Sensitivity Matrix to turn localized term distortions into active cash arbitrage. When continuous sensors detect a localized terminal hazard hump peaking at a KRD vector of 18.55 at the 50-year node, the system programmatically activates a sub-national corporate tax-exempt multiplier τm=.021 alongside automated interest rate swap overlays. This systematic adjustment compresses the raw borrowing cost down to an optimized 3.792%, structurally flattening the annual debt service denominator.
By pairing these liability-side optimization layers with locked fixed-price 24/7 carbon-free Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and federal policy anchors under IRS Section 45U ($15.00/MWh PTC), the algorithm establishes an airtight capital shield. Pushed through a high-throughput 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo grid simulation core, the re-engineered framework mathematically demonstrates a secure steady-state convergence at a 1.65 Mean DSCR, completely flattens empirical default probabilities to a flawless 0.0000%, and secures $26.53 Million in net annual savings directly back to the public treasury.

title: Privacy for Sale: Anarchy, Ban, or Market?
affiliations: Northwestern University - Department of Economics, Columbia University and Columbia University - Columbia Business School

detail.title: Privacy for Sale: Anarchy, Ban, or Market?
detail.abstract: Third-party data sharing is a widespread practice whereby firms acquire consumer data as a by-product of ordinary transactions and then sell it to other market participants, potentially imposing privacy costs on consumers. We study this practice in a framework with a monopolistic seller, a privately informed consumer, and a third party who chooses how intensively to utilize the data acquired from the seller. Our analysis highlights the role of the privacy β, which captures whether consumers with a higher willingness to pay for the seller's product are more (β > 0) or less (β ≤ 0) averse to greater data use. When β > 0, third-party data sharing is coarse: the seller collects and sells at most one data record, pooling consumer types. In this case, greater data use lowers consumer rents. Conversely, when β ≤ 0, third-party data sharing is granular: the seller collects and sells multiple records that reveal consumer types. In this case, greater data use increases consumer rents. These forces govern the welfare comparison among three policy regimes: data anarchy, a data ban, and a data market.

title: Adjust Quantity or Adjust Wages? Monetary Policy Shocks, Financing Constraints, and Corporate Labor Demand
affiliations: , East China Normal University (ECNU), Shandong Management University, Zhejiang University of Technology and East China Normal University (ECNU)

detail.title: Adjust Quantity or Adjust Wages? Monetary Policy Shocks, Financing Constraints, and Corporate Labor Demand
detail.abstract: How does monetary policy affect labor market outcomes through the firm demand side? We build a directed-search model in which firms jointly choose vacancy posting quantities and posted wages under financial frictions, and test the model’s predictions using online job posting data from Chinese publicly listed firms spanning 2016-2024, identified via local projections (LP). We find that: (1) a contractionary monetary policy shock generates a persistent and statistically significant decline in both the number of job postings and the probability of hiring, whereas the dynamic responses of posted wages exhibit no consistent sign; (2) firms with lower asset tangibility, higher trade credit dependence, and higher interest-bearing debt ratios experience substantially larger contractions in hiring quantities; (3) high-skill and high-wage positions contract more sharply after a tightening shock, consistent with their higher total recruitment costs; (4) heterogeneity analysis reveals differentiated responses by ownership type, firm age, and industry; (5) across all mechanism tests and heterogeneity dimensions, wage adjustments display no significant cross-sectional differences. This uniform absence of wage adjustment heterogeneity indicates that wage stickiness is a pervasive structural friction on the labor demand side, rather than a feature limited to particular firm types. Our findings carry implications for understanding the microeconomic transmission of monetary policy and for assessing the long-run effects of financing frictions on firms’ human capital investment.

title: Production Networks and Systemic Tail Risk: A Structural Asset-Pricing Model

detail.title: Production Networks and Systemic Tail Risk: A Structural Asset-Pricing Model
detail.abstract: The strongest buyer and supplier relationships are also the ones with the largest excess return co-movement. We develop a structural asset pricing model that maps this dependence into closed form measures of systemic co-risk. In Compustat data, linked firms exhibit a 0.079 correlation premium: weak links resemble unlinked pairs, while the strongest carry a premium of 0.16. The premium resides primarily in shared market and industry co-movement. Through the model, it raises ∆CoVaR by one to two percentage points. Among firms with positive footprints, the top decile accounts for 43% of the total.

title: Evaluating the Economic and Public Health Efficacy of Multi-Pollutant Mitigation Policies

detail.title: Evaluating the Economic and Public Health Efficacy of Multi-Pollutant Mitigation Policies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing financial or personal interests influencing this study.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by H Heuristics under its digital‑economy research initiative.

detail.abstract: Climate policy and air-quality policy are scored on different ledgers, then added as an afterthought called a cobenefit. The public files show they occupy the same geography. Of 198 scored countries, 86 sit in a joint cellpopulation-weighted PM2.5 at or above the WHO interim target of 15 micrograms per cubic metre, and a fossil grid (fossil electricity at least 50 percent, or coal at least 10). Those 86 countries hold 5.76 billion people, 71 percent of the sample population, 80 percent of implied air-pollution deaths, and 67 percent of territorial carbon dioxide. The health-only cell-dirty air on a clean grid-holds 0.77 billion people and 14 percent of the deaths, with 1.3 percent of the carbon. The climate-only cell-clean air on a fossil grid-holds 0.94 billion people, 4 percent of the deaths, and 25 percent of the carbon. Efficacy is a cell result, not a pollutant result. Between 2010 and the latest year, 139 of 176 growing countries with data cut PM2.5; 54 of 175 cut territorial carbon. The end-of-pipe signature, particles down and carbon still up, describes 68 countries and 3.22 billion people, led by China: exposure from 49 to 32 micrograms, coal's share of electricity from 77 to 58 percent, carbon up 43 percent. The source-control signature, both series down, describes 43 countries and 1.18 billion people, concentrated in the OECD. Fifteen countries levy an emissions-weighted carbon tax of at least ten dollars a tonne; two of them sit in the joint cell. On the World Bank adjusted-savings accounts, particulate damage exceeds carbon damage only in low-income economies, where the median co-benefit ratio is 1.58 and the median air-pollution death rate is 208 per 100,000 against 18 in highincome economies. The dollar ledger understates the health case where the deaths are, because the value of a statistical life scales with income. A multi-pollutant policy is a source-control policy aimed at the joint cell. Everything else is a single-pollutant policy wearing a co-benefit label.

title: Extending Market-abuse Surveillance across Related Products: A Factor-based Framework
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Extending Market-abuse Surveillance across Related Products: A Factor-based Framework
detail.abstract: Market-abuse surveillance often asks whether suspicious activity in one instrument moved its price and benefited a position in that same instrument. That logic can miss cases in which the economically beneficial position is held in a different but related product. This paper develops a factor-based framework for two practical tasks that arise once a source-instrument impact has already been estimated: identifying which other products should be reviewed and constructing a benchmark for the potential benefit in those products. The method represents instruments by their exposures to common market factors, uses those exposures to discover related products without requiring manually specified peer lists, and then projects the factor-driven component of the source movement onto each target product. The projected target movement is combined with signed account exposure to estimate potential economic benefit. A controlled simulation shows that the method recovers a known factor-related target and also illustrates why a purely instrument-specific source shock should not be treated as broadly transferable. A public-market illustration with 465 U.S. equities further shows that an Exxon Mobil (XOM)-centered search retrieves economically coherent energy-related firms without using sector labels. The closest peers remain stable across alternative PCA retention choices and overlap substantially, but not completely, with rankings based on raw return correlation. This agreement supports the economic plausibility of the discovery method, while the differences reflect its focus on commonrisk exposures rather than raw co-movement. The framework is intended as a scalable screening and factor-consistent attribution benchmark, not as a causal estimate or legal determination of market abuse.

reference: No.
title:
The Behavioral Migration Model:
 A Multi-level Process Theory of Behavioral Change, Economic Transformation, and Capital Reallocation

detail.title:
The Behavioral Migration Model:
 A Multi-level Process Theory of Behavioral Change, Economic Transformation, and Capital Reallocation
detail.abstract: The Behavioral Migration Model (BMM) is proposed as a multi-level process theory explaining how technological innovation may contribute to long-term economic transformation through changes in recurring human and organizational behavior. The model distinguishes relatively stable recurring societal functions from the evolving methods used to perform them and identifies Behavioral Migration as the point at which a technology-enabled method becomes the dominant and socially expected behavior within a defined population. The theory integrates insights from innovation diffusion, technology acceptance, socio-technical transitions, innovation resistance, evolutionary economics, structural transformation, and capital-allocation research. It proposes a cyclical process in which technological innovation creates behavioral alternatives; perceived value and behavioral resistance shape adoption and normalization; Behavioral Migration is followed by Economic Migration; and sustained economic reorganization may contribute to Capital Reallocation, which can in turn support subsequent innovation. The model does not claim that its individual constructs are wholly novel. Its proposed contribution lies in integrating and ordering established insights within a behaviorcentered, multi-level architecture that links technological possibility to societal normalization, economic restructuring, and financial reallocation. The paper develops theoretical propositions, boundary conditions, and a future research agenda for empirical testing and refinement of the model.

title: A Structural Coverage Buffer and the Cross-Section of Bank Failures

detail.title: A Structural Coverage Buffer and the Cross-Section of Bank Failures
detail.abstract: A structural model of fire sales in banking implies a solvency boundary that separates banks whose mapped asset base covers outside funding from those whose mapped asset base does not. We map this theory-derived boundary to U.S. commercial bank balance sheets and evaluate it against realized failures. Four quarters before failure, coverage falls short for 49 percent of failed-bank observations against 16 percent of contemporaneous at-risk observations in the same quarters, and the gap persists in the full sample and outside the Global Financial Crisis period. Conditional on the accounting mapping, the zero cutoff is fixed by the model's solvency condition rather than selected to maximize failure discrimination. The empirically informative feature is whether the boundary is crossed. This classification is invariant to how a fixed asset base is split into liquid and harder-to-liquidate legs, so it does not depend on the accounting partition. Distance from the boundary is far less robust, being partition-sensitive and carrying only weak-to-moderate within-state information. The undercovered state is not absorbing: about one-third of undercovered bank-quarter observations return above the line the following quarter. A valuation extension highlights a different source of fragility among the 2023 interest-rate-loss cases: marking held-to-maturity securities to market lowers the asset base itself. Consistent with its role as a broad summary of bank solvency, the book capital ratio provides stronger overall failure discrimination. The structural boundary instead supplies a theory-imposed cutoff within an explicitly defined balance-sheet mapping.

title: Weighting Uncertainty in Egypt-Africa Logistics-Hub Assessment: A BWM-TOPSIS Robustness Study

detail.title: Weighting Uncertainty in Egypt-Africa Logistics-Hub Assessment: A BWM-TOPSIS Robustness Study
detail.abstract: Multi-criteria logistics-hub assessments can produce seemingly precise rankings even when candidate ordering is sensitive to contested weighting assumptions. This study evaluates weighting uncertainty rather than attempting to select a location. Ten named candidate labels are compared through a fully synthetic decision matrix covering market and port access, inland connectivity, security, green performance, distributor reach, skills, reverse logistics, and land cost. A balanced Best–Worst Method/TOPSIS reference scenario is compared with market-led, green-circular, and security-resilience weight structures. Reference-scenario scores range from 0.352 to 0.604, while Spearman correlations with alternative scenarios range from 0.552 to 0.964. The variation demonstrates that candidate ordering is not invariant to strategic priorities. The contribution is a robustness workflow for diagnosing weight dependence, rank reversal, and evidence requirements. No site is recommended because the values are generated and no audited GIS, financial, environmental, or stakeholder data were used.

title: The Economics of Clean Technology Diffusion: How Low-Carbon Innovation Spreads across Economies

detail.title: The Economics of Clean Technology Diffusion: How Low-Carbon Innovation Spreads across Economies
detail.abstract:
Cost collapse is treated as diffusion. It is not. Solar photovoltaic levelised cost in the IRENA world series fell from
42 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2010 to 4 cents in 2024. Modules fell from 2.44 dollars per watt to 26 cents. Solar’s
share of world electricity rose from 0.15 percent to 6.9 percent. That is a real clock. It is a traded-goods clock. In a
balanced reading of Ember and Energy Institute generation files, IRENA capacity, and the IEA Global EV Data
Explorer via Our World in Data, the extensive margin closed and the intensive margin did not. Among countries
with a 2024 generation file, 77 percent had crossed 1 percent solar, against 1.5 percent in 2010. Forty-eight percent
had crossed 5 percent, against none. On a 217-country latest-available cross-section, 58 percent are extensive on
solar and 31 percent are intensive, meaning 5 percent of electricity on a grid that already reaches 80 percent of the
population. China holds 48 percent of installed solar capacity, against 2.5 percent in 2010, and 39 percent of solar
terawatt-hours. Sub-Saharan Africa holds 13 gigawatts and 10 watts per person, against 505 watts in high-income
economies. Developing-country solar’s share of electricity is uncorrelated with income. Watts per person is not.
Electric vehicles occupy a third map. China is 53 percent of new car sales and 65 percent of world units. Nepal is 68
percent of a thin car market at 0.9 percent solar. The United States is 10 percent electric on 17 percent solar-plus-
wind. Nine developing countries occupy a hardware club — intensive on at least two of solar, wind, and electric
vehicles — covering 1.98 billion people, of which China is 1.41 billion. Fifty-one developing countries occupy
none. IEA Energy Technology Perspectives puts China’s share of clean-technology manufacturing value at
about 70 percent, modules above 80, wafers at 95. A cheap module is not a watt. A watt is not a system. Low-carbon
innovation spreads as manufactured hardware sitting on complementary capital. Treating Wright’s law as a diffusion
law is how a price gets counted as African adoption.

title: The Relationship Between Organizational Employees and their Leaders Mildo dos Santos

detail.title: The Relationship Between Organizational Employees and their Leaders Mildo dos Santos
detail.abstract: The relationship between employees and leaders plays a crucial role in organizational performance and the internal climate of a company. Effective leadership can promote employee engagement, increase job satisfaction, and stimulate professional development, creating an environment of mutual trust and collaboration. Assertive communication, when used clearly and objectively, is essential to avoid misunderstandings and strengthen the bond between leaders and teams. In addition, recognition of individual and collective employee efforts contributes to maintaining high motivation, demonstrating that the work performed is valued. Leaders who are able to inspire their teams become agents of change and transformation, capable of aligning employees' personal objectives with organizational goals. However, when relationships between leaders and subordinates are fragile or poorly managed, conflicts, demotivation, and even increased turnover may arise, harming the work environment and company results. Investing in the continuous development of leadership competencies, as well as in the construction of an inclusive and participatory organizational culture, is fundamental to strengthening these relationships. In this way, it is possible to create a space where trust, collaboration, and alignment of objectives are constant elements, promoting the organization's sustainable success.

title: The Lean Government How Governments Can Move at AI Speed without being Governed by AI

detail.title: The Lean Government How Governments Can Move at AI Speed without being Governed by AI
detail.abstract: Governments are adopting artificial intelligence inside institutions designed for a slower technological and administrative era. The immediate gains are real, but automating documents, searches, and workflows does not resolve the deeper constraint: institutional latency, the time and friction between a change in society and the state's ability to understand it, decide, act, measure consequences, and correct course. This article proposes the Lean Government as an operating model for closing that gap. Its cycle is Sense, Simulate, Decide, Deliver, Measure, and Correct. It also identifies an emerging deployment gap between frontier capability and institutional adoption. Closing it requires a translation layer that can connect public missions, model capabilities, secure architecture, procurement, workflow redesign, workforce adoption, evaluation, and accountable authority. Artificial intelligence can strengthen every stage, but public authority must remain human, lawful, contestable, and accountable. Society scale simulation should become an instrument of public reasoning, not a source of sovereignty. The decisive competition in government AI will concern institutional capacity and mission delivery, not model access alone.

title: Calibration-Aware Conditional Synthetic Augmentation under Explicit Feasibility Constraints: Repeated Validation on Mobile and Sensor Miscarriage-Risk Records
affiliations: Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca - UNIVERSITA' DI MILANO BICOCCA,  and University of Milano-Bicocca

detail.title: Calibration-Aware Conditional Synthetic Augmentation under Explicit Feasibility Constraints: Repeated Validation on Mobile and Sensor Miscarriage-Risk Records

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No Funding received for this research.

detail.abstract: Synthetic tabular data are increasingly used for augmentation and privacyoriented data access, but their value for probabilistic risk prediction cannot be inferred from distributional resemblance or discrimination alone. We evaluated a calibration-aware conditional synthetic augmentation framework for miscarriage-risk prediction from repeatedly collected mobile and healthcaresensor records. A conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty was conditioned on the binary outcome and prespecified age and body-mass-index strata. Its objective combined adversarial learning with moment matching, correlation preservation, raw-domain feasibility, and label-consistency penalties. Generative and predictive hyperparameters were selected on a dedicated tuning partition using constrained Bayesian optimization and then locked for 20 repeated held-out evaluations. In each repetition, elastic-net logistic models were fitted to real records alone or to real plus 4,000 synthetic records. Recalibration was estimated only from a separate real-data calibration partition, and all metrics were evaluated on held-out real records. Synthetic augmentation did not change discrimination: mean AUC was 0.641 for both training strategies, with a paired difference of 0.000 (0.000, 0.000). It produced small improvements in Brier score (-0.001), log loss (-0.002), absolute calibration-slope error (-0.248), and 10-bin equal-width ECE (-0.071). Tie-preserving 10-bin ACE decreased by -0.007, but its resampling interval included zero (-0.016 to 0.002; adjusted Wilcoxon p = 0.751). Differences largely disappeared after Platt or temperature calibration. No Bayesian-optimization candidate satisfied all feasibility constraints; mean classifier two-sample-test AUC was 0.612, mean pre-projection domain-violation rate was 87.5%, and the nearest-neighbour memorization proxy was 0.022%. Conditional augmentation therefore acted as a modest regularizer for the uncalibrated predictor, but it neither improved ranking nor yielded a generator that naturally respected the prespecified feature domain. Because the data comprise repeated records and were split at record level, the findings are methodological and do not establish clinical deployment readiness.

title: Three-Layer Climate Risk Absorption in China's Corporate Bond Market: Diagnostic Evidence from Interbank Medium-Term Notes

detail.title: Three-Layer Climate Risk Absorption in China's Corporate Bond Market: Diagnostic Evidence from Interbank Medium-Term Notes
detail.abstract: We study the institutional channels through which climate risk is absorbed before reaching the primary-market coupon of Chinese interbank medium-term notes (MTNs). We develop a three-layer absorption framework—credit ratings, third-party guarantees, and implicit state support—and implement its diagnostic protocol on a fully public, reproducible 12-city prototype that combines 4,130 NOAA station-day weather records for 2024 with 1,667,274 ChinaBond rating-curve observations for 2020–2025. Three results emerge. First, rating-implied funding costs are sharply compressed at the AAA end (2.23–2.31%) and dispersed at the A end (8.56–10.90%), mirroring the issuer-level rating compression documented for the 1,468-MTN universe. Second, physical climate exposure sorts significantly across all three institutional layers: AAA status, state ownership, and guarantee flags each separate climate risk at the 5% level, and all three comparisons survive Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Third, a one-standard-deviation increase in physical climate risk is associated with a 3.01-percentage-point higher rating-implied coupon (R² = 0.67; HC1 p < 0.001) that is robust across seven pre-specified variations of the extreme-day thresholds, the yield tenor, the polar-city sample, mid-tier rating assignments, and CRI weights, and the guarantee and rating interactions carry the predicted negative absorption signs. A 5,000-draw placebo permutation confirms that the interaction sign template is not an artifact of arbitrary flag assignment, while making explicit that confirmatory interaction inference requires the 1,468-MTN companion sample. The results locate the climate-pricing null of primary markets in the rating–guarantee–ownership architecture rather than in investor inattention, with direct implications for disclosure-based climate policy.

title: Adaptive Governance under Climate Stress: Institutions that Update Policies Dynamically as Environmental Conditions Shift

detail.title: Adaptive Governance under Climate Stress: Institutions that Update Policies Dynamically as Environmental Conditions Shift
detail.abstract:
Adaptive governance is emerging as a necessary replacement for legacy, static policy systems that cannot keep pace with accelerating climate volatility, technological disruption, and interconnected global crises. As the document states, “traditional, static policy frameworks [are] obsolete” under conditions of non‑linear environmental change and systemic polycrisis.

This report develops a quantitative macro‑systems model in which governance behaves as a continuously computing algorithm rather than a fixed legal manuscript. Institutions integrate biophysical sensor networks, multi‑agent AI orchestration, and parametric policy triggers to minimize reaction latency and maintain system symmetry. Key mechanisms include automated fiscal stabilizers, dynamic zoning linked to real‑time sea‑level telemetry, algorithmic energy‑grid pricing, and autonomous agricultural redundancy protocols. These systems emulate the thermodynamic efficiency of biological networks by processing environmental feedback continuously and adapting locally before global failure cascades occur.

The document outlines a phased 2026–2050 roadmap transitioning institutions from sensor‑driven “shadow systems” to fully symmetrical macro‑systems capable of autonomous policy execution. Case studies across coastal resilience, energy grids, and agriculture demonstrate how dynamic policy updating reduces systemic risk, compresses economic shocks, and leverages cost‑curve declines in compute and sensor technologies to make adaptive governance feasible even for emerging economies.

title:
Leader Self-Interest and Self-oriented Behavior: 
A Conceptual Study of Constructive and Destructive Leadership

detail.title:
Leader Self-Interest and Self-oriented Behavior: 
A Conceptual Study of Constructive and Destructive Leadership
detail.abstract: Leadership research has mainly focused on task-oriented and people-oriented leadership behaviors. However, leaders are also influenced by their own personal and professional interests, such as career growth, reputation, job security, recognition, promotion, and status. Existing research has examined related ideas, including self-serving and exploitative leadership. These studies have generally focused on the harmful effects of leaders putting their own interests before others. This paper takes a broader conceptual approach. It examines Self-Oriented Behavior (SOB) as leadership behavior influenced by a leader's own personal or professional interests. The paper proposes that self-oriented behavior does not necessarily produce the same outcome in every situation. It may produce constructive outcomes when the leader's self-interest encourages behavior that also benefits employees or the organization. It may produce destructive outcomes when the pursuit of self-interest harms employees, the organization, or other stakeholders. The paper proposes a conceptual relationship between situational conditions, leader selfinterest, Self-Oriented Behavior, and organizational and employee outcomes. It also proposes that Self-Oriented Behavior can exist together with task-oriented and people-oriented behaviors. The paper does not claim that leader self-interest is a completely new area of research. Instead, it proposes a way to examine the relationship between leader self-interest, leadership behavior, context, and consequences. Future empirical research is needed to determine whether Self-Oriented Behavior can be reliably distinguished from existing leadership constructs.

title: How Network Effects Shape Firm Entry Strategies

detail.title: How Network Effects Shape Firm Entry Strategies
detail.abstract: There is a common presumption that network effects intensify firms' race to enter first as they seek to secure an incumbency advantage. We explore this possibility in an infinite-horizon model in which two vertically differentiated firms decide whether and when to enter a growing market.
